definition_zh: 献身于；致力于；把（时间、精力、资源）专用于；虔诚奉献
definition_en: to give one's self, time, or resources wholly to a person, cause, or purpose
core_image: 一条许愿的绳结：把整个人系在一件事上
scene: 深夜实验室里，研究员把周末都留在培养皿和记录表旁。 The researcher devoted the whole weekend to a set of failed experimental data in the lab at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 devote 是「投入、专用于」（第 2 个义项：把时间精力给某件事）；句意：研究员在深夜的实验室里，把整个周末都投入到一组失败的实验数据上。

pos.zh: 献身于；致力于；把……专用于

senses.title: Bind by a vow: dedicate to a god
senses.definition: to set something apart for a god or a sacred purpose by a solemn promise
senses.definitionCN: 通过庄严承诺把某物划出，献给神或神圣用途
senses.example: The chapel was devoted to Saint Anne.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小教堂献给了圣安妮。
senses.why: Latin devotus is the past participle of devovere, 'to vow away': de- 'away' plus vovere 'to vow'. A thing vowed is taken out of ordinary use and handed to a higher purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 devotus 是 devovere 的过去分词，意为“许愿献出”：de-“离开”+ vovere“许愿”。许愿之物被从日常用途中取出，交给更高的目的。

senses.title: Give time and energy to a task
senses.definition: to give a large amount of time and effort to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 把大量时间和精力投入到某项活动
senses.example: The team devoted months to the design.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为这个设计投入了几个月。
senses.why: By c. 1600 the vow image had widened: what is handed over need not be a sacred object but can be hours and effort, offered exclusively to one task.
senses.whyCN: 到约 1600 年，誓愿意象扩大了：交出的不必是圣物，也可以是小时与精力，专门供给一项任务。

senses.title: Devote oneself to a cause
senses.definition: to commit your whole self to a person, cause, or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 把整个自己投入到一个人、事业或生活方式中
senses.example: She devoted herself to public health.
senses.exampleCN: 她投身于公共卫生事业。
senses.why: The reflexive form makes the self the offering. Instead of giving a thing, the speaker gives their own life, so commitment becomes personal identity.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把“自我”当作供品。说话者给的不再是一件东西，而是自己的人生，于是承诺变成个人身份。

senses.title: Set money or resources aside for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 把资金或资源专拨给某用途
senses.definition: to reserve money, materials, or effort for one specific use
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、材料或精力专门留给一种用途
senses.example: One percent of income was devoted to research.
senses.exampleCN: 收入的百分之一被专拨给研究。
senses.why: A budget is a set of boundaries. Devoting a sum marks it off from general spending, the same way a vowed object is marked off from ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 预算是一组边界。把一笔钱 devote 出来，就是把它从一般开支中划出，如同许愿之物被从日常用途中划出。

senses.title: Give a life or career to something
senses.titleCN: 把一生或职业生涯献给某事
senses.definition: to spend your entire working life on one field, person, or service
senses.definitionCN: 把全部职业生涯用于一个领域、一个人或一项服务
senses.example: She devoted forty years to teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 她把四十年献给了教学。
senses.why: A life is the largest unit a person can hand over. When the object is a career, the vow reaches its maximum duration and the word sounds like a vocation.
senses.whyCN: 一生是一个人能交出的最大单位。当对象是职业生涯时，誓愿达到最长时段，这个词听起来就像一种天职。

senses.title: Devote attention or study to something
senses.definition: to focus your attention or study on one subject
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力或研究集中在某一主题
senses.example: Devote your attention to the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 把注意力集中在第一段。
senses.why: Attention is a limited resource, so giving it to one thing means withdrawing it from others. The word's exclusiveness is what makes devotion feel intense.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是有限资源，给了一件事就意味着从别处收回。这个词的排他性正是“投入”显得强烈的原因。

senses.title: Give a space or building to a use
senses.titleCN: 把场所或建筑用于某用途
senses.definition: to set apart a room, building, or area for one function
senses.definitionCN: 把房间、建筑或区域划给一种功能
senses.example: The old hall was devoted to a library.
senses.exampleCN: 旧礼堂被改作图书馆。
senses.why: A building can be vowed to a use: its doors are opened for one purpose only. The physical boundary makes the old religious sense visible again.
senses.whyCN: 建筑可以被“许愿”给一种用途：它的门只为一种目的打开。物理边界让古老的宗教义再次可见。

senses.title: Be devoted: hold a steady loyalty
senses.titleCN: 忠于：保持稳定的情感联结
senses.definition: in the phrase be devoted to, to love and support someone steadily
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be devoted to，表示稳定地爱与支持某人
senses.example: He is devoted to his students.
senses.exampleCN: 他对学生十分关爱。
senses.why: The past participle freezes the vow into a continuing state. Devoted is no longer the act of promising but the steady bond that the promise left behind.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词把誓愿凝固成持续状态。devoted 不再是许诺的动作，而是许诺留下的稳定纽带。

senses.title: Doom or consign to harm (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 注定遭祸；交托给毁灭（古义）
senses.definition: in 17c.–18c. usage, to consign someone or something to destruction
senses.definitionCN: 在 17–18 世纪的用法中，把某人或某物交托给毁灭
senses.example: In old usage a ship could be devoted to the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧用法中，一条船可以被“交托”给礁石。
senses.why: The 1640s sense was 'doom, consign to some harm or evil'. Johnson's Dictionary (1755) lists 'to curse, to doom to destruction'. The same handover can aim at a god or at ruin.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 40 年代的义项是“注定、交托给某种伤害或邪恶”。约翰逊词典（1755）列有“诅咒、注定毁灭”。同一种交出，可以朝向神，也可以朝向毁灭。

intro.en: Devote entered English through the language of vows: to devote was first to set something apart by a solemn promise. It later warmed into steady commitment, and for a time it also meant to doom.
intro.cn: devote 经由“誓愿”的语言进入英语：最初指以庄严承诺把某物分别出来，后来转暖为稳定的投入，也一度表示“注定毁灭”。

items.en: First recorded as 'appropriate by or as if by vow'; by c. 1600 it meant 'apply zealously or exclusively', and by the 1640s 'doom, consign to harm'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 80 年代，义为“以誓愿奉献”；约 1600 年转为“热切或专门投入”，17 世纪 40 年代又出现“注定遭祸”的用法。

items.en: From Latin devotus, past participle of devovere 'dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly', built from de- 'down, away' + vovere 'to vow'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 devotus，即 devovere 的过去分词，意为“以誓愿奉献、献出自己、庄严承诺”，由 de-“向下、离开”+ vovere“许愿”构成。

items.en: vovere produced votum 'solemn promise', the source of vote, vow, and votive. The deeper PIE root *wegwh- 'to speak solemnly' is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: vovere 生成 votum“庄严承诺”，是 vote、vow、votive 的来源。更深层的原始印欧语词根 *wegwh-“庄严地说”属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: In the 18th century the word often carried a negative tone. Johnson's Dictionary (1755) lists 'to addict, to give up to ill' and 'to curse, to doom to destruction'.
items.cn: 18 世纪这个词常带负面色彩。约翰逊词典（1755）列出“沉溺、献身于恶”和“诅咒、注定毁灭”两个义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the warm sense in devote oneself to and devoted, while dedicate stresses a formal external act and consecrate stresses making sacred.
items.cn: 现代英语在 devote oneself to 与 devoted 中保留温暖的义项；dedicate 强调正式的外部行为，consecrate 强调使之神圣。

note.en: The first group is about similar spelling and sound; the second is about words that also mean giving yourself or something to a purpose.
note.cn: 第一组看拼写和读音，第二组看同样表示“把自己或某物交给某个目的”的词。

entries.definition: to eat something quickly and greedily. It looks close but comes from de- + vorare 'to swallow'.
entries.definitionCN: 狼吞虎咽地吃。词形相近，但来自 de- + vorare“吞下”。

entries.definition: deeply religious. It is the same Latin participle devotus, borrowed through French.
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的。它正是同一个拉丁分词 devotus，经法语借入。

entries.definition: a very enthusiastic follower. It is a noun made from devote, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 狂热爱好者。它是由 devote 构成的名词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to set something apart for a serious purpose, especially with a ceremony. It stresses the external act.
entries.definitionCN: 为严肃目的（尤以仪式）把某物划出专用。它强调外部行为。

entries.definition: to make something sacred by a religious rite. It is narrower and more sacred than devote.
entries.definitionCN: 通过宗教仪式使某物神圣。它比 devote 更窄、更神圣。

entries.definition: to promise time, money, or yourself to something. It stresses the binding promise rather than the gift.
entries.definitionCN: 承诺投入时间、金钱或自身。它强调约束性的承诺，而非献出。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the image of vovere 'to vow', the participle devotus 'vowed away', the difference from dedicate, and the everyday pattern devote something to something.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：vovere“许愿”的意象、分词 devotus“许愿献出”、与 dedicate 的差别，以及 devote something to something 的日常搭配。

normal.en: Latin vovere means 'to vow'. To devote is to make a vow with your life as the offering.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vovere 意为“许愿”。devote 就是拿自己的人生作供品的许愿。

normal.en: Devotus is 'vowed away': de- 'away' plus vovere 'vow' — the thing is set apart from ordinary use.
normal.cn: devotus 是“许愿献出”：de-“离开”+ vovere“许愿”——该物被从日常用途中划出。

normal.en: Dedicate is the public ceremony; devote is the inner commitment. You can dedicate a building but devote your life.
normal.cn: dedicate 是公开仪式，devote 是内在承诺。你可以 dedicate 一栋楼，却 devote 一生。

normal.en: The pattern devote something to something fixes the target: time to research, a chapter to grammar, a fund to repairs.
normal.cn: devote something to something 固定了对象：时间给研究、一章给语法、资金给维修。

normal.en: Devoted keeps the vow alive: a devoted nurse is still bound to her patients by care.
normal.cn: devoted 让誓愿持续生效：a devoted nurse 仍以关怀系于病人。

abstract.en: A vow is a boundary: it takes one thing out of the many possible uses and gives it to one purpose.
abstract.cn: 誓愿是一条边界：它把一件事从多种可能用途中取出，只给一个目的。

abstract.en: Devotion turns quantity into identity: not how much time you give, but that you have given yourself.
abstract.cn: 献身把数量变成身份：重点不是给出多少时间，而是你已经把自己交了出去。

abstract.en: The same logic can invert: handing a person over to harm was once 'devoting' them. Commitment and doom share one structure.
abstract.cn: 同一逻辑可以反转：把人交给毁灭也曾叫 devote。承诺与注定毁灭共享一个结构。

examples.en: She devoted her career to marine biology.
examples.cn: 她把职业生涯献给了海洋生物学。

examples.en: The first chapter is devoted to grammar.
examples.cn: 第一章专门讲语法。

examples.en: He is devoted to his students.
examples.cn: 他对学生十分关爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: “得 vote”——把每一票都投给它 → devote 献身、致力于

root: 拉丁语 devovere“以誓愿献出”，由 de-“离开”+ vovere“许愿”构成；同族有 vow、vote、votum。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of devote, all built on one act: handing something over by a vow. The object can be a god, a cause, time, money, a building, or one's whole life.
sensesIntro.cn: devote 的九个义项都建立在一个动作上：以誓愿把某物交出。交出的对象可以是神、事业、时间、金钱、建筑，乃至整个生命。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vow that ties a person to one purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把人系在单一目的上的誓愿。

branches.en: VOW: the Latin root is a solemn promise that sets a thing apart for a god or a purpose.
branches.cn: 许愿：拉丁词根是把某物分别出来献给神或某个目的的庄严承诺。

branches.en: GIVE WHOLLY: time, energy, and the self are handed over as if by vow.
branches.cn: 完全交出：时间、精力与自我像许愿一样被交出去。

branches.en: RESERVE: money, space, or a building is marked off exclusively for one use.
branches.cn: 专留：金钱、空间或建筑被划出来只供一种用途。

branches.en: ATTACH LOYALLY: a life, attention, or a lasting bond is fastened to a person or craft.
branches.cn: 忠诚附着：一生、注意力或持久纽带被系在一个人或一门手艺上。

branches.en: DOOM: the same handing-over could mean consigning someone to harm, a sense now archaic.
branches.cn: 注定：同一种“交出”也可指把人交托给毁灭，此义已古旧。

intro.en: Devote is a Latin verb that English expanded with -ed, -ee, -ion, and -al. The base vovere also gave vow and vote through related Latin nouns.
intro.cn: devote 是拉丁动词，英语用 -ed、-ee、-ion、-al 扩展它。词根 vovere 还经由相关拉丁名词生成 vow 与 vote。

latinIntro.en: Latin devovere 'vow away' and devotus 'vowed' sit beside votum 'vow' and votivus 'promised by a vow'. Devout is the same participle borrowed through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 devovere“许愿送出”与 devotus“已许愿的”，旁边是 votum“誓愿”和 votivus“还愿的”。devout 正是同一个分词经法语借入。

items.meaning: giving loyalty and love to someone or something
items.meaningCN: 忠诚的；挚爱的（-ed 分词作形容词）

items.meaning: a person who is very enthusiastic about something
items.meaningCN: 热衷者；信徒（-ee 表示人）

items.meaning: deep love, loyalty, or religious commitment
items.meaningCN: 献身；虔诚（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: relating to religious worship
items.meaningCN: 灵修的；虔诚的（-al 构成形容词）

items.meaning: deeply religious; sincerely felt
items.meaningCN: 虔诚的；衷心的（同一拉丁分词经法语传入）

items.meaning: in a deeply religious or sincere way
the quality of being loyal and loving
items.meaningCN: 忠诚；挚爱（-ness 构成抽象名词）
items.exampleCN: 她的忠诚打动了所有人。

items.meaning: the giving of one's own life or effort to a cause
items.meaningCN: 自我奉献（self + devotion 复合）

items.meaning: the act of devoting; dedication

latinEntries.meaning: to dedicate by a vow; promise solemnly
a solemn promise to a god; a vow, a wish
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对神的庄严承诺；誓愿、心愿

latinEntries.meaning: promised by a vow; given in fulfilment of a vow

definition_zh: 区分；辨别；使不同；分化；求微分
definition_en: to recognize or make a difference between things, or to develop into a specialized form
core_image: 两件几乎相同的东西被一条细线分开
scene: 显微镜下，两张载玻片上的细胞看起来几乎一样。 Under the microscope the student differentiated the two kinds of cells that looked the same.
sceneCN: 这里 differentiate 是「区分、辨别」（第 1 个义项：看出两者的差异）；句意：显微镜下，学生区分开了两种看起来相同的细胞。

pos.zh: 区分；辨别；使不同；求微分

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 区分开

senses.title: Tell two things apart
senses.definition: to recognize that two things are not the same
senses.definitionCN: 看出两件事物并不相同
senses.example: Consumers cannot differentiate the two brands.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者无法区分这两个品牌。
senses.why: The Latin noun differentia means 'difference'. The verb's non-technical sense, recorded in 1876, is simply the mental act of drawing that difference.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 differentia 意为“差异”。1876 年记录的日常义，就是把这个差异在头脑里画出来。

senses.title: Make one thing distinct from another
senses.definition: to be the feature that makes two things distinguishable
senses.definitionCN: 成为让两物可被区别的特征
senses.example: Color differentiates the male from the female.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色把雄性与雌性区分开来。
senses.why: differre is 'to carry apart': dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry'. A feature that separates two things literally carries them away from each other.
senses.whyCN: differre 意为“分开携带”：dis-“分开”+ ferre“携带”。把两物分开的特征，字面上就是把它们各自带走。

senses.title: Develop into a specialized type
senses.definition: in biology, to develop from a general cell into a specialized one
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，由普通细胞发育成专门细胞
senses.example: Cells differentiate into muscle, nerve, or bone.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞分化成肌肉、神经或骨骼细胞。
senses.why: The intransitive sense 'acquire a distinct and separate character' appeared in 1874. Biology took it literally: a cell takes on a separate identity.
senses.whyCN: 不及物义“获得独特而分离的性质”出现于 1874 年。生物学把它按字面使用：细胞获得了独立的身份。

senses.title: Make a product or brand different
senses.definition: to give a product a feature that sets it apart in a market
senses.definitionCN: 给产品一个在市场中被区别出来的特征
senses.example: The company differentiates its phones by camera quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司用相机质量让手机与众不同。
senses.why: Marketing extends 'make different' to competitive identity: the brand must be carried apart from every rival in the buyer's mind.
senses.whyCN: 市场营销把“使不同”扩展到竞争身份：品牌必须在买家心中与所有对手分开。

senses.title: Distinguish right from wrong
senses.definition: to draw a moral or conceptual line between categories
senses.definitionCN: 在类别之间划出道德或概念界线
senses.example: Children learn to differentiate right from wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子学会分辨是非。
senses.why: A judgment is a line between two categories. The same act that separates species or brands also separates acceptable from unacceptable.
senses.whyCN: 判断就是两个类别之间的一条线。区分物种或品牌的动作，也区分可接受与不可接受。

senses.title: Treat people differently
senses.definition: to apply different standards to people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者群体适用不同标准
senses.example: The law must not differentiate between rich and poor.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不得区别对待穷人与富人。
senses.why: When the line drawn between categories becomes unequal treatment, the verb takes a social and often negative sense. The difference stops being neutral.
senses.whyCN: 当类别之间画出的线变成不平等待遇，这个词就带上社会性、常为负面的含义。差异不再中立。

senses.title: Calculate a derivative
senses.definition: in mathematics, to find the derivative of a function
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，求一个函数的导数
senses.example: Differentiate the function with respect to x.
senses.exampleCN: 对该函数关于 x 求导。
senses.why: This is the word's first home: the 1816 mathematical sense. A derivative measures the rate at which a function changes, so the verb names the operation that extracts that rate.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早的家：1816 年的数学义。导数衡量函数变化的速率，动词就指提取该速率的运算。

senses.title: Separate kinds in classification
senses.definition: to mark off species or types by their differences
senses.definitionCN: 按差异把物种或类型划开
senses.example: Taxonomists differentiate species by wing pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 分类学家按翅纹区分物种。
senses.why: Classification is literal marking-off, the oldest core of the word. Each category is a patch separated from its neighbours by a visible trait.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是字面上的“划开”，是这个词最古老的核心。每个类别都是被可见特征与邻居分开的一块。

senses.title: Differentiate oneself
senses.definition: to make yourself stand out from others by a distinct quality
senses.definitionCN: 以独特之处使自己与他人分开
senses.example: She differentiated herself through original research.
senses.exampleCN: 她以原创研究让自己脱颖而出。
senses.why: The reflexive form makes the person the object that is set apart. The line is now drawn between the self and the crowd, not between two external things.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把人自己变成被划出的对象。这条线现在画在“自我”与人群之间，而不是两个外部事物之间。

intro.en: Differentiate was born in calculus and only later moved into ordinary judgment. Its parts are dis- 'apart' and ferre 'carry', the same verb behind transfer and refer.
intro.cn: differentiate 生于微积分，后来才进入日常判断。它的构件是 dis-“分开”与 ferre“携带”，后者也是 transfer、refer 的动词。

items.en: First recorded as a transitive verb in mathematics, 'obtain the differential coefficient of'.
items.cn: 最早记录为数学及物动词，义为“求出微分系数”。

items.en: From differentiatus, past participle of differentiare, from Latin differentia 'diversity, difference'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 differentiatus，即 differentiare 的过去分词，源头是拉丁语 differentia“差异、不同”。

items.en: differentia comes from differre 'to set apart', from dis- 'apart' + ferre 'to bear, carry' (PIE *bher- 'to carry').
items.cn: differentia 来自 differre“分开携带”，由 dis-“分开”+ ferre“承载、携带”构成（原始印欧语 *bher-“携带”）。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'acquire a distinct and separate character' appears, later central to biology.
items.cn: 不及物义“获得独特而分离的性质”出现，后来成为生物学的核心用法。

items.en: The non-technical transitive sense 'discriminate between by observing or describing the difference' is recorded.
items.cn: 非技术性的及物义“通过观察或描述差异来辨别”被记录。

note.en: The first group is about shared spelling and sound; the second is about verbs that also separate one thing from another.
note.cn: 第一组看共同的拼写与读音，第二组看同样把一物与另一物分开的动词。

entries.definition: to be unlike. It is the shorter verb behind difference and different.
entries.definitionCN: 不同；有差异。它是 difference 与 different 背后的短动词。

entries.definition: not the same. It is the adjective built on Latin differre.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的。它是建立在拉丁语 differre 上的形容词。

entries.definition: relating to a difference, especially in mathematics or mechanics.
entries.definitionCN: 与差异有关的，尤用于数学或机械。

entries.definition: to recognize or show a difference, often with careful attention. It is broader and more formal than differentiate.
entries.definitionCN: 认出或表明差异，常含仔细留意。它比 differentiate 更宽、更正式。

entries.definition: to perceive a difference, or to treat unfairly. The word carries a strong social sense that differentiate usually lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉差异，或作不公平对待。它带有 differentiate 通常没有的强烈社会含义。

entries.definition: to move things apart or keep them apart. It stresses physical distance rather than perceived difference.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分开或隔开。它强调物理距离，而非被感知的差异。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin parts dis- + ferre, the 1816 calculus origin, biological differentiation, and the 1876 everyday sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁构件 dis- + ferre、1816 年的微积分来源、生物分化，以及 1876 年的日常义。

normal.en: differre is dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry': to differentiate is to carry two things apart in your mind.
normal.cn: differre 是 dis-“分开”+ ferre“携带”：differentiate 就是在头脑里把两物各自带走。

normal.en: The word started in calculus in 1816; a derivative is the rate extracted from a changing function.
normal.cn: 这个词 1816 年始于微积分；导数就是从变化函数中提取出的速率。

normal.en: Cells differentiate: one general cell becomes a separate, specialized kind.
normal.cn: 细胞分化：一个普通细胞变成独立而专门的种类。

normal.en: In 1876 the verb moved into ordinary speech: observe a difference and name it.
normal.cn: 1876 年这个词进入日常语言：观察差异并把它说出来。

normal.en: The reflexive pattern differentiate oneself draws the line between you and the crowd.
normal.cn: 反身搭配 differentiate oneself 把线画在你与人群之间。

abstract.en: Difference is a relation, not a thing: the line exists because someone draws it between two items.
abstract.cn: 差异是一种关系，不是实物：线之所以存在，是因为有人在两项之间画了它。

abstract.en: Specialization is narrowing: to become distinct, a cell gives up other possible identities.
abstract.cn: 专门化就是收窄：为了变得独特，一个细胞放弃了其他可能的身份。

abstract.en: The same separating act can be neutral (classification) or unjust (discrimination). The line itself does not decide its ethics.
abstract.cn: 同一种分开动作可以是中立的（分类），也可以是不义的（歧视）。线本身并不决定其伦理。

examples.en: Consumers cannot differentiate the two brands.
examples.cn: 消费者无法区分这两个品牌。

examples.en: Cells differentiate into muscle, nerve, or bone.
examples.cn: 细胞分化成肌肉、神经或骨骼细胞。

examples.en: She differentiated herself through original research.
examples.cn: 她以原创研究让自己脱颖而出。

dict_mnemonic.text: “different 加 -iate”——先看见 different（不同），再动手去分 → differentiate 区分

root: 拉丁语 differre“分开携带”，由 dis-“分开”+ ferre“携带”构成；名词 differentia 即“差异”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of differentiate, all built on one act: drawing a line between two things. The line can be perceptual, physical, biological, commercial, moral, or mathematical.
sensesIntro.cn: differentiate 的九个义项都建立在一个动作上：在两物之间画线。这条线可以是感知的、物理的、生物的、商业的、道德的或数学的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine line drawn between two nearly identical things.
core.cn: 核心意象：在两个几乎相同的事物之间画一条细线。

branches.en: SEE: the first move is mental — noticing that two things differ, or judging that a line must not be crossed.
branches.cn: 看见：第一步是心智动作——注意到两物不同，或判断某条界线不可逾越。

branches.en: MARK OFF: a visible trait, a classification rule, or a social standard separates one group from another.
branches.cn: 划开：可见特征、分类规则或社会标准，把一类与另一类分开。

branches.en: SPECIALIZE: in biology the separated part develops its own identity.
branches.cn: 专门化：在生物学中，被分开的部分发展出自己的身份。

branches.en: STAND OUT: in markets and careers, the line is drawn between a product or person and the crowd.
branches.cn: 脱颖而出：在市场与职业中，线画在产品或个人与人群之间。

branches.en: CALCULUS: the original mathematical operation extracts a rate of change.
branches.cn: 微积分：最早的数学运算提取变化速率。

intro.en: Differentiate is built from the Latin noun differentia plus the verb suffix -ate. English then adds -tion, -tion, and the negative prefix un- to make a whole family.
intro.cn: differentiate 由拉丁名词 differentia 加动词后缀 -ate 构成。英语再用 -tion 与否定前缀 un- 扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin differre 'carry apart' yields differens 'different' and differentia 'difference'; English also keeps the participle stem in different and differential.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 differre“分开携带”生成 differens“不同的”和 differentia“差异”；英语还在 different、differential 中保留分词词干。

items.meaning: not the same as another
items.meaningCN: 不同的（-ent 构成形容词）

items.meaning: the quality or state of being unlike
items.meaningCN: 差异；不同（-ence 构成名词）

items.meaning: relating to a difference; a small difference in amount
items.meaningCN: 微分的；差别的；差额（-ial 后缀）

items.meaning: the act of distinguishing, or the process of specialization
items.meaningCN: 区分；分化（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: able to be differentiated, especially in mathematics
items.meaningCN: 可微分的；可区分的（-able 表示能够）

items.meaning: made distinct, or developed into specialized forms
not yet specialized or separated into kinds
items.meaningCN: 未分化的；未区分的（un- 表否定）

items.meaning: having no interest or concern; neither good nor bad
items.meaningCN: 漠不关心的；平庸的（in- 表否定，词义已转移）

items.meaning: lack of interest or concern
in another way
items.exampleCN: 他们对问题的看法不同。

definition_zh: 维度；尺寸；方面；规模；层面
definition_en: a measurable direction or extent, or one aspect of a situation
core_image: 一把量尺同时量出长、宽、高三个方向
scene: 设计师在屏幕上旋转三维模型，旁边放着一把量尺。 The designer rotated the model on the screen to check its proportions in all three dimensions.
sceneCN: 这里 dimension 是「维度、尺寸」（第 1 个义项：可测量的方向）；句意：设计师在屏幕上旋转模型，检查它在三个维度上的比例。

senses.title: A measurable direction in space
senses.definition: one of the directions in which a space or object can be measured, such as length, width, or height
senses.definitionCN: 空间或物体可被度量的方向之一，如长、宽、高
senses.example: A cube has three dimensions.
senses.exampleCN: 立方体有三个维度。
senses.why: Latin dimensio is 'a measuring', from dimetiri 'measure out'. The first English sense was 'measurable extent', so a dimension is literally a direction along which measurement is taken.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dimensio 意为“测量”，来自 dimetiri“量出”。英语最早义为“可测量的范围”，所以 dimension 字面上就是量尺所沿的方向。

senses.title: Size or extent of an object
senses.definition: the size of something, especially its length, width, and height
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小，尤指长、宽、高
senses.example: The dimensions of the room surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 房间的尺寸让我们吃惊。
senses.why: Once several directions are measured, their results become the object's dimensions. The word moves from the act of measuring to the numbers produced.
senses.whyCN: 一旦量出几个方向，结果就成为物体的 dimensions。这个词从测量动作转到测量所得的数值。

senses.title: An aspect of a situation
senses.definition: one part or feature of a complex situation
senses.definitionCN: 复杂情况中的一个部分或特征
senses.example: The issue has a political dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题有政治层面。
senses.why: The 1929 sense 'any component of a situation' treats a problem as a space with several directions. Each aspect is a separate axis along which the case can be examined.
senses.whyCN: 1929 年出现的“情况的任一组成部分”把问题当作有多个方向的空间。每个方面都是审视该问题的一条独立轴线。

senses.title: A level of experience
senses.definition: a level or quality that enriches an experience
senses.definitionCN: 丰富某种体验的层次或品质
senses.example: Music adds an emotional dimension to the film.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐为影片增添了情感层面。
senses.why: A film can be measured along more than one axis: plot, image, sound, feeling. Calling emotion a dimension says it is a whole direction of experience, not a decoration.
senses.whyCN: 影片可以沿不止一条轴度量：情节、画面、声音、情感。把情感称为 dimension，是说它是体验的一整个方向，而非装饰。

senses.title: A coordinate in physics
senses.definition: one of the independent coordinates needed to describe a physical event
senses.definitionCN: 描述物理事件所需的独立坐标之一
senses.example: Time is treated as a fourth dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 时间被当作第四维。
senses.why: Physics turns the measuring directions into coordinates. A point in space-time needs four numbers, so the axes become dimensions in the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把测量方向变成坐标。时空中的一点需要四个数，因此这些轴成为技术意义上的维度。

senses.title: The number of coordinates in mathematics
senses.definition: the number of independent coordinates needed to locate a point in a space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间中定位一点所需的独立坐标数
senses.example: The space has dimension four.
senses.exampleCN: 这个空间是四维的。
senses.why: Mathematics abstracts the count: dimension is no longer a physical direction but the minimum number of numbers needed to specify a position.
senses.whyCN: 数学把“数量”抽象出来：维数不再是物理方向，而是确定一个位置所需的最少数字个数。

senses.title: Measurements written down
senses.definition: the measured sizes of an object, used for fitting or building
senses.definitionCN: 物体的测量尺寸，用于装配或建造
senses.example: Check the dimensions before ordering the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 订书架前先核对尺寸。
senses.why: In practical use the plural dimensions names the set of measurements a builder or buyer needs. The abstract directions become a list of numbers.
senses.whyCN: 在实际使用中，复数 dimensions 指建造者或买家需要的那组测量值。抽象方向变成了一串数字。

senses.title: Scale of a problem or change
senses.definition: the size or seriousness of a problem, especially when it is large
senses.definitionCN: 问题的大小或严重程度，尤指规模很大时
senses.example: Few grasped the dimensions of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人看清这场危机的规模。
senses.why: A crisis is also a space: its dimensions are how far it reaches in each direction. 'Scale' is the extent measured along every axis at once.
senses.whyCN: 危机也是一个空间：它的 dimensions 是它在各个方向上延伸多远。“规模”就是同时沿每条轴量出的范围。

senses.title: A realm or universe
senses.definition: a separate realm or order of reality, especially in speculative writing
senses.definitionCN: 独立的领域或现实层次，尤见于想象性作品
senses.example: The story opens a door to another dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 故事打开了一扇通往另一个维度的门。
senses.why: By 1912 dimension was used for a whole realm or universe. If space can have extra axes, another set of axes can be imagined as another world.
senses.whyCN: 到 1912 年，dimension 被用来指整个领域或宇宙。如果空间可以有额外轴，另一组轴就可以被想象成另一个世界。

intro.en: Dimension is a measuring word. Latin dimetiri meant 'measure out', and the noun dimensio named the act; English first used it for measurable extent, then for aspects of a situation.
intro.cn: dimension 是一个测量词。拉丁语 dimetiri 意为“量出”，名词 dimensio 指这一动作；英语先用它表示可测范围，再扩展到情况的各个方面。

items.en: dimensioun 'measurable extent, magnitude measured along a diameter' is recorded.
items.cn: 记录到 dimensioun，义为“可测范围、沿直径量得的量值”。

items.en: From dimensionem, noun of action from dimetiri 'to measure out', dis- + metiri 'to measure'.
items.cn: 来自 dimensionem，是 dimetiri“量出”的动名词，由 dis- + metiri“测量”构成。

items.en: metiri belongs to PIE *me- 'to measure', the root behind meter, measure, and metre.
items.cn: metiri 属于原始印欧语 *me-“测量”，是 meter、measure、metre 的共同词根。

items.en: The sense 'bulk, size, extent, capacity' develops.
items.cn: “体积、大小、范围、容量”的义项出现。

items.en: The word is used for a realm or universe, as in 'another dimension'.
items.cn: 该词被用来指领域或宇宙，如“另一个维度”。

items.en: The modern sense 'any component of a situation' is recorded.
items.cn: 现代义“情况的任一组成部分”被记录。

note.en: The first group is about similar form and sound; the second is about words that also name size, extent, or an aspect.
note.cn: 第一组看词形与读音，第二组看同样表示大小、范围或方面的词。

entries.definition: a reduction in size or importance. It begins with the same dimi- but comes from minuere 'make small'.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或重要性的减少。同样以 dimi- 开头，但来自 minuere“使变小”。

entries.definition: relating to dimensions. It is the adjective from dimension, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 与维度有关的。它是 dimension 的形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: having dimensions of a stated kind, as in 'a small-dimensioned room'.
entries.definitionCN: 具有某类尺寸的，如“小尺寸房间”。

entries.definition: the area or degree to which something reaches. It stresses coverage rather than measurable axes.
entries.definitionCN: 某物延伸的面积或程度。它强调覆盖范围，而非可测的轴。

entries.definition: one part or side of a situation. It is close to dimension in the 1929 sense but does not imply measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或侧面。它接近 1929 年义的 dimension，但不含测量意味。

entries.definition: the great size or importance of something. It names the scale itself, not the directions that produce it.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的巨大或重要程度。它指规模本身，而不是产生规模的各个方向。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin parts dis- + metiri, the 1520s size sense, the 1929 sense 'aspect', and the 1912 sense 'another dimension'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁构件 dis- + metiri、1520 年代的尺寸义、1929 年的“方面”义，以及 1912 年的“另一维度”义。

normal.en: dimetiri is dis- 'apart' plus metiri 'measure': to dimension is to measure out along each separate direction.
normal.cn: dimetiri 是 dis-“分开”+ metiri“测量”：dimension 就是沿每个分开的方向分别量出。

normal.en: A cube needs three numbers: length, width, height. Those three directions are its dimensions.
normal.cn: 立方体需要三个数：长、宽、高。这三个方向就是它的维度。

normal.en: A problem also has dimensions: political, economic, emotional. Each is an axis you can measure the case along.
normal.cn: 问题也有维度：政治的、经济的、情感的。每条都是审视该问题的一条轴。

normal.en: In mathematics dimension is a count of coordinates, not a physical direction.
normal.cn: 数学中的 dimension 是坐标的数量，不是物理方向。

normal.en: 'Another dimension' works because if space has extra axes, another set of axes can be imagined as another world.
normal.cn: “另一个维度”之所以成立，是因为如果空间有额外轴，另一组轴就可以被想象成另一个世界。

abstract.en: A dimension is a question you can ask of an object: how long? how wide? how heavy? Each question is an axis.
abstract.cn: 维度是你能对物体提出的一个问题：多长？多宽？多重？每个问题都是一条轴。

abstract.en: To name an aspect a dimension is to say it is not a detail but a whole direction of the thing.
abstract.cn: 把一个方面称为 dimension，是说它不是细节，而是该事物的一整个方向。

abstract.en: Reality may be described with more axes than we can perceive; the word allows new axes to become new worlds.
abstract.cn: 现实或许能用比我们所能感知的更多轴来描述；这个词允许新轴变成新世界。

examples.en: A cube has three dimensions: length, width, and height.
examples.cn: 立方体有三个维度：长、宽、高。

examples.en: The issue has an important political dimension.
examples.cn: 这个问题有重要的政治层面。

examples.en: Music adds an emotional dimension to the film.
examples.cn: 音乐为影片增添了情感层面。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地门神”——地门神站在三个方向量门框 → dimension 维度、尺寸

root: 拉丁语 dimetiri“量出”，由 dis-“分开”+ metiri“测量”构成；名词 dimensio 即“测量、量度”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of dimension, all built on one act: measuring along an axis. The axis can be physical, mathematical, emotional, political, or a whole imagined world.
sensesIntro.cn: dimension 的九个义项都建立在一个动作上：沿一条轴测量。这条轴可以是物理的、数学的、情感的、政治的，或整个想象世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measuring rod turning to measure length, width, and height at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把量尺转着量出长、宽、高三个方向。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a dimension is a measurable direction, then a coordinate, then a count of coordinates.
branches.cn: 科学：维度先是可测方向，再是坐标，最后是坐标的数量。

branches.en: SIZE: the measured directions produce the object's size, written down as dimensions.
branches.cn: 尺寸：量出的方向产生物体的大小，写成尺寸数据。

branches.en: ASPECT: a situation is treated as a space, and each component becomes an axis.
branches.cn: 方面：情况被当作空间，每个组成部分成为一条轴。

branches.en: LEVEL: an experience can gain a whole new direction, such as emotion.
branches.cn: 层面：一种体验可以获得全新的方向，例如情感。

branches.en: REALM: extra axes are imagined as another universe.
branches.cn: 领域：额外轴被想象成另一个宇宙。

intro.en: Dimension is a Latin noun. English adds -al, -ally, -less, and the prefix multi- to build its family.
intro.cn: dimension 是拉丁名词。英语给它加 -al、-ally、-less，以及前缀 multi- 来构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin dimensio 'a measuring' comes from dimetiri, whose second element metiri also gives meter and measure. The participle stem is dimension-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dimensio“测量”来自 dimetiri，其第二构件 metiri 也生成 meter 与 measure。分词词干是 dimension-。

items.meaning: relating to dimension or dimensions
items.meaningCN: 维度的；尺寸的（-al 构成形容词）

items.meaning: with respect to dimensions
having no units or dimensions, as in physics
having dimensions of a specified kind
the state or number of dimensions
items.meaningCN: 维数；维度性（-ity 构成抽象名词）

items.meaning: having many dimensions or aspects
items.meaningCN: 多维的；多方面的（multi- 表“多”）

items.meaning: flat, having only length and width; also, lacking depth
items.meaningCN: 二维的；平面的（也喻指缺乏深度）

items.meaning: having length, width, and height; solid
the act of marking measurements on a drawing

definition_zh: 减少；缩小；削弱；贬低；减轻
definition_en: to become or make smaller, weaker, or less important
core_image: 一块方糖在水里越缩越小
scene: 烛台上的蜡烛越烧越短，墙上的影子慢慢拉长。 As the candle burned shorter, the light on the wall diminished.
sceneCN: 这里 diminish 是「变小、减弱」（第 5 个义项：声音或光减弱）；句意：随着蜡烛越烧越短，墙上的光逐渐减弱。

senses.title: Become smaller or less
senses.definition: to become smaller in size, amount, or number
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或数目上变小
senses.example: The lake diminished over the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖在夏天渐渐变小。
senses.why: The verb is a merger of two old words built on Latin minuere 'make small'. The intransitive sense, recorded in the 1510s, lets the thing itself grow less without an agent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由两个建立在拉丁语 minuere“使变小”的古词合并而成。1510 年代记录的不及物义，让事物自身变少，无需施动者。

senses.title: Make something smaller
senses.definition: to reduce the size or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 减小某物的大小或数量
senses.example: The drug diminishes appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药会降低食欲。
senses.why: With a direct object the same root becomes transitive: an outside cause makes the thing less. English inherited both the transitive and intransitive patterns from its two source verbs.
senses.whyCN: 带直接宾语时，同一词根转为及物：外部原因使事物变少。英语从两个来源动词继承及物与不及物两种模式。

senses.title: Reduce power or importance
senses.definition: to make someone or something less powerful or important
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物权力更小、重要性更低
senses.example: The scandal diminished his authority.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻削弱了他的权威。
senses.why: The mid-15c sense was 'lower in power, importance, or estimation'. Power is treated as a quantity that can be made smaller, like a pile of grain.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期的义项是“降低权力、重要性或评价”。权力被当作一种可以变小的量，像一堆谷物。

senses.title: Reduce value or worth
senses.definition: to make something worth less, especially money or assets
senses.definitionCN: 使某物价值更低，尤指金钱或资产
senses.example: Inflation diminishes savings.
senses.exampleCN: 通货膨胀使储蓄贬值。
senses.why: Value is measured on a scale, and a smaller position on the scale is a diminished value. The word's measuring origin survives in this economic use.
senses.whyCN: 价值是在尺度上度量的，尺度上的位置更小就是价值被降低。这个词的测量出身在经济用法中保留下来。

senses.title: Fade in strength
senses.definition: to become weaker in sound, light, or force
senses.definitionCN: 声音、光线或力量变弱
senses.example: The noise diminished as the train left.
senses.exampleCN: 火车远去，噪声逐渐减弱。
senses.why: A sound has no fixed size, but it has intensity. Diminish treats intensity as an amount that can shrink until the sound disappears.
senses.whyCN: 声音没有固定大小，但有强度。diminish 把强度当作可以缩小、直到声音消失的量。

senses.title: Belittle a person
senses.definition: to make a person seem less important or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 使某人显得不那么重要或有价值
senses.example: He never missed a chance to diminish her.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不放过贬低她的机会。
senses.why: The same act of lowering can be applied to a person's standing. To diminish someone is to reduce their perceived size in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“降低”可以施加于人的地位。贬低某人，就是缩小他在别人眼中的分量。

senses.title: Lessen pain or risk
senses.definition: to reduce the intensity of pain, danger, or a bad effect
senses.definitionCN: 降低痛苦、危险或不良影响的强度
senses.example: Proper care diminishes the risk of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 适当护理能降低感染风险。
senses.why: Risk and pain are quantities of harm. Diminish is the neutral verb for making them smaller; it does not remove them entirely, only lowers the amount.
senses.whyCN: 风险与痛苦是“伤害的量”。diminish 是使它们变小的中性动词；它不彻底消除，只降低数量。

senses.title: Reduce a musical interval
senses.definition: in music, to lower an interval by a semitone, producing a diminished chord or interval
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中把音程缩小半音，形成减音程或减和弦
senses.example: The chord uses a diminished fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个和弦用了减五度。
senses.why: Music borrowed the visual idea of shrinking: an interval that is one semitone smaller than its natural form is 'diminished', as if a measured length were cut short.
senses.whyCN: 音乐借用了“缩小”的视觉意象：比自然形式小一个半音的音程被称为“减的”，仿佛一段被截短的长度。

senses.title: Diminishing returns
senses.definition: in economics, the phrase for the point where extra effort yields less and less benefit
senses.definitionCN: 经济学用语，指额外投入带来的收益越来越少
senses.example: Each extra hour brings diminishing returns.
senses.exampleCN: 每多投入一小时，收益都在递减。
senses.why: The phrase treats benefit as a quantity that shrinks with each additional unit of effort. Diminish names the direction of the curve, not a one-time loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把收益当作随每增加一单位投入而缩小的量。diminish 指曲线的走向，而非一次性损失。

intro.en: Diminish is a double heritage: two Old French verbs, both from Latin words for 'make small', merged into one English verb in the early 15th century.
intro.cn: diminish 是双重遗产：两个古法语动词都来自拉丁语“使变小”，在 15 世纪初合并成一个英语动词。

items.en: diminishen appears as a merger of two obsolete verbs, diminue and minish.
items.cn: diminishen 出现，是两个已废弃动词 diminue 与 minish 的合并。

items.en: diminue comes from Old French diminuer and Latin diminuere 'break into small pieces', a variant of deminuere 'lessen'.
items.cn: diminue 来自古法语 diminuer 与拉丁语 diminuere“打碎成小块”，后者是 deminuere“减少”的变体。

items.en: minish comes from Old French menuisier and Latin minuere 'make small'.
items.cn: minish 来自古法语 menuisier 与拉丁语 minuere“使变小”。

items.en: deminuere = de- 'completely' + minuere 'make small', from PIE *mei- 'small'.
items.cn: deminuere = de-“完全”+ minuere“使变小”，源自原始印欧语 *mei-“小”。

items.en: The sense 'lower in power, importance, or estimation' appears.
items.cn: “降低权力、重要性或评价”的义项出现。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'grow less, become or appear smaller' is recorded.
items.cn: 不及物义“变少、变小或显得更小”被记录。

note.en: The first group is about shared beginnings or endings; the second is about verbs that also make something less.
note.cn: 第一组看相同的词首或词尾，第二组看同样使某物变少的动词。

entries.definition: a measurable direction or aspect. It shares the dimi- opening but comes from metiri 'measure'.
entries.definitionCN: 可测的方向或方面。同样以 dimi- 开头，但来自 metiri“测量”。

entries.definition: extremely small; also a word form expressing smallness. It comes from the same minuere family.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；也指表示“小”的词形。它出自同一个 minuere 词族。

entries.definition: to destroy a building completely. It rhymes in -ish but comes from demoliri, not minuere.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底拆毁建筑。词尾 -ish 押韵，但来自 demoliri，而非 minuere。

entries.definition: to become or make less in number or size. It is the most neutral partner of diminish.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或大小上变少。它是最中性的 diminish 近义词。

entries.definition: to make something smaller, often deliberately. It stresses an agent and a method.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变小，常为有意为之。它强调施动者与方法。

entries.definition: to make pain, risk, or an effect smaller. It is close to diminish but usually takes an abstract object.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻痛苦、风险或影响。它接近 diminish，但常接抽象宾语。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the two merged verbs, the Latin minuere 'make small', the 1510s intransitive sense, and musical diminished intervals.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：两个合并的动词、拉丁语 minuere“使变小”、1510 年代的不及物义，以及音乐中的减音程。

normal.en: Two Old French verbs, diminue and minish, both meant 'make small'. English merged them into diminish.
normal.cn: 两个古法语动词 diminue 与 minish 都表示“使变小”。英语把它们合并成 diminish。

normal.en: The Latin core is minuere 'make small'; minimum and minor belong to the same smallness family.
normal.cn: 拉丁核心是 minuere“使变小”；minimum 与 minor 属于同一个“小”的词族。

normal.en: Intransitive use came in the 1510s: a lake can diminish by itself, without anyone shrinking it.
normal.cn: 不及物用法出现于 1510 年代：湖泊可以自己变小，无需别人去缩。

normal.en: Power and value are treated as amounts: to diminish someone is to lower their position on a scale.
normal.cn: 权力与价值被当作数量：贬低某人就是降低他在尺度上的位置。

normal.en: A diminished chord is one semitone 'cut short', the same shrinking image applied to sound.
normal.cn: 减和弦就是被“截短”一个半音，同一个缩小意象用在声音上。

abstract.en: Diminish is quantitative: it lowers an amount without asking whether the remainder is still enough.
abstract.cn: diminish 是量化的：它降低数量，却不问剩下的是否仍然够用。

abstract.en: The same verb covers physical shrinkage, social standing, value, and intensity: all are amounts on some scale.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖物理缩小、社会地位、价值与强度：它们都是某种尺度上的量。

abstract.en: Belittling is shrinking a person in other minds, which shows how easily a measuring word becomes a moral one.
abstract.cn: 贬低就是在他人心中缩小一个人，可见一个测量词多么容易变成道德词。

examples.en: The lake diminished over the summer.
examples.cn: 这个湖在夏天渐渐变小。

examples.en: The drug diminishes appetite.
examples.cn: 这种药会降低食欲。

examples.en: Each extra hour brings diminishing returns.
examples.cn: 每多投入一小时，收益都在递减。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of diminish, all built on one image: a quantity shrinking. The quantity can be size, power, value, sound, pain, or benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: diminish 的九个义项都建立在一个意象上：数量缩小。这个量可以是大小、权力、价值、声音、痛苦或收益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar cube shrinking smaller and smaller in water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块方糖在水里越缩越小。

branches.en: SIZE: the core physical sense, intransitive or transitive.
branches.cn: 大小：核心的物理义，可及物也可不及物。

branches.en: STATUS AND VALUE: power and worth are amounts on a social or economic scale.
branches.cn: 地位与价值：权力与价值是社会或经济尺度上的量。

branches.en: FORCE AND HARM: sound fades and pain or risk is lowered.
branches.cn: 力量与伤害：声音减弱，痛苦或风险被降低。

branches.en: BELITTLE: the same lowering is applied to a person's standing.
branches.cn: 贬低：同一种降低施加于人的地位。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND PHRASE: music cuts an interval short; economics names a curve of shrinking benefit.
branches.cn: 技术与短语：音乐把音程截短；经济学命名一条收益缩小的曲线。

intro.en: Diminish is a verb from Latin minuere. English adds -ed, -ing, -tion, and -ive, and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: diminish 是来自拉丁语 minuere 的动词。英语加 -ed、-ing、-tion、-ive，以及否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin minuere 'make small' yields minutus 'small' and the noun minuere family behind minimum, minor, and minute. Deminuere adds de- 'completely'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minuere“使变小”生成 minutus“小的”，以及 minimum、minor、minute 背后的词族。Deminuere 加上 de-“完全”。

items.meaning: made smaller or weaker; also, a musical interval reduced by a semitone
items.meaningCN: 减少的；减弱的；（音乐）减音程的

items.meaning: becoming less; often used in 'diminishing returns'
items.meaningCN: 逐渐减少的；“收益递减”常用

able to be reduced

items.meaningCN: 渐弱（音乐术语，源自拉丁语“减少”）

definition_zh: 直接的；直的；指导；导演；指向；直率的
definition_en: going straight without deviation, or to guide, aim, or manage something
scene: 片场上，摄影机、监视器和场记板都已就位。 The director stood on the set and directed the actor to walk toward the window.
sceneCN: 这里 direct 是「导演、指导」（第 6 个义项：监督电影或戏剧的制作）；句意：导演站在片场，指导演员朝窗边走。

最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Straight, without turning
senses.definition: going in a straight line or by the shortest route
senses.definitionCN: 沿直线或最短路线前进
senses.example: We took a direct flight to Tokyo.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乘直飞航班去东京。
senses.why: Latin directus is the past participle of dirigere 'set straight'. The adjective entered English around 1400 with exactly that shape: a line with no bend in it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 directus 是 dirigere“使直”的过去分词。形容词约 1400 年进入英语，正是这个形状：一条没有弯的线。

senses.title: Point or aim something
senses.definition: to aim or turn something toward a target
senses.definitionCN: 把某物瞄准或转向目标
senses.example: She directed the beam at the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 她把光束对准墙壁。
senses.why: From c. 1400 the verb meant 'point or aim in a straight line toward a place or object'. A straight line from hand to target is the same geometry as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 约 1400 年起，动词意为“沿直线指向某地或某物”。从手到目标的直线，与形容词是同一种几何。

senses.title: Guide or supervise
senses.definition: to guide a person, group, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个人、群体或活动
senses.example: He directs the research group.
senses.exampleCN: 他领导这个研究组。
senses.why: By the early 15c direct meant 'govern, regulate as to behavior, prescribe the course of'. A director keeps others on a chosen line.
senses.whyCN: 到 15 世纪初，direct 意为“治理、规范行为、规定路线”。导演或主管就是让别人保持在选定的线上。

senses.title: Give an order
senses.definition: to tell someone officially what to do
senses.definitionCN: 正式告诉某人该做什么
senses.example: The officer directed them to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 警官指示他们离开。
senses.why: The 1650s sense 'order, ordain' turns guidance into authority. The straight line becomes an instruction: go this way, not that way.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 50 年代义“命令、规定”把引导变成权威。直线变成指令：走这边，不走那边。

senses.title: Address words or mail to someone
senses.definition: to send a letter or remark to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 把信件或话语发送给特定的人
senses.example: Direct your complaint to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的投诉写给经理。
senses.why: The oldest English sense, late 14c, was 'write or address a letter or words to someone'. A message is aimed along a line toward one recipient.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早义（14 世纪晚期）是“把信或话写给某人”。信息沿一条线射向一个收件人。

senses.title: Supervise a film or play
senses.definition: to control the making of a film, play, or similar production
senses.definitionCN: 控制电影、戏剧或类似作品的制作
senses.example: She directed three films.
senses.exampleCN: 她执导了三部电影。
senses.why: The 1913 sense 'supervise and control the making of' extends the manager role to film. The director sets the line that the whole production follows.
senses.whyCN: 1913 年义“监督并控制制作”把管理者角色扩展到电影。导演设定整部作品遵循的那条线。

senses.title: Candid and plain
senses.definition: honest and clear, without evasion
senses.definitionCN: 诚实清楚，不回避
senses.example: He gave a direct answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了直截了当的回答。
senses.why: From the 1580s direct meant 'plain, expressive, not ambiguous'. Straight speech is speech with no detour, the same image applied to language.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 80 年代起，direct 意为“明白、清楚、不含糊”。直话就是不绕路的语言，同一意象用在言语上。

senses.title: Immediate, without a middle step
senses.definition: happening or working without an intermediary
senses.definitionCN: 无需中间人即发生或起作用
senses.example: You have direct access to the files.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以直接访问这些文件。
senses.why: A direct route has no stop; a direct link has no middle node. The spatial 'no detour' becomes procedural 'no intermediary'.
senses.whyCN: 直达路线没有停靠；直连没有中间节点。空间上的“不绕路”变成程序上的“无中介”。

senses.title: Electric current in one direction
senses.definition: of electric current, flowing continuously in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 电流持续沿一个方向流动
senses.example: Direct current flows from the battery to the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 直流电从电池流向电路。
senses.why: The adjective keeps its literal geometry: current that does not alternate or reverse, but moves along one straight direction.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留字面几何：不交替、不反向，只沿一个直线方向流动的电流。

intro.en: Direct is a straight-line word. Latin dirigere 'set straight' gave both the adjective and the verb, and English extended the line to guidance, orders, letters, films, and electric current.
intro.cn: direct 是一个直线词。拉丁语 dirigere“使直”同时生成形容词与动词，英语把这条线扩展到指导、命令、信件、电影与电流。

items.en: directen means 'to write or address a letter or words to someone', and also 'to point out a course'.
items.cn: directen 意为“把信或话写给某人”，也表示“指出路线”。

items.en: The adjective means 'straight, undeviating, not crooked'.
items.cn: 形容词义为“直的、不偏离的、不弯曲的”。

items.cn: directus 是 dirigere“使直、引导”的过去分词，由 dis-“分开”+ regere“保持笔直”构成（原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”）。

items.en: 'Govern, regulate as to behavior, prescribe the course of actions' develops.
items.cn: “治理、规范行为、规定行动路线”的义项出现。

items.en: The sense 'order, ordain' is recorded.
items.cn: “命令、规定”的义项被记录。

items.en: 'Supervise and control the making of a play or film' is attested.
items.cn: “监督并控制戏剧或电影制作”的义项被记录。

note.cn: 第一组看 direct 词族与形近词，第二组看同样表示引导或瞄准的动词。

entries.definition: in a direct way; also, immediately. It is the adverb from direct.
entries.definitionCN: 直接地；也指立即。它是 direct 的副词。

entries.definition: a person who directs an organization or a film.
entries.definitionCN: 主管；导演。指指导组织或影片的人。

entries.definition: a list of names or files; originally a book of directions.
entries.definitionCN: 名录；文件目录。原指“指导手册”。

entries.definition: to show someone the way, especially through a place. It stresses accompanying rather than ordering.
entries.definitionCN: 给人带路，尤指穿过某地。它强调陪同，而非命令。

entries.definition: to control the direction of a vehicle or process. It keeps the straight-line image but adds active control.
entries.definitionCN: 控制车辆或过程的方向。它保留直线意象，但增加主动操控。

entries.definition: to organize and lead an activity, or to lead musicians. It is more formal than direct in management.
entries.definitionCN: 组织并领导活动，或指挥音乐。作管理义时比 direct 更正式。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin regere 'keep straight', the 1400 adjective, the 1913 film sense, and the literal direct current.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 regere“保持笔直”、1400 年的形容词、1913 年的电影义，以及字面的直流电。

normal.en: dirigere is dis- 'apart' plus regere 'keep straight': direct means keeping something on one line.
normal.cn: dirigere 是 dis-“分开”+ regere“保持笔直”：direct 就是让某物保持在一条线上。

normal.en: The adjective came around 1400: a direct flight draws a line with no stop.
normal.cn: 形容词约 1400 年出现：直飞航班画出一条没有停靠的线。

normal.en: A director keeps a group or a film on the chosen line, which is why guidance and film-making share one word.
normal.cn: 导演让剧组或影片保持在选定的线上，这就是“指导”与“拍片”共用一个词的原因。

normal.en: Direct speech has no detour: the meaning travels straight from speaker to listener.
normal.cn: 直话没有绕路：意思从说话者直线到达听者。

normal.en: Direct current literally moves one way; alternating current reverses, so it is not direct.
normal.cn: 直流电字面上只朝一个方向；交流电会反向，所以不是 direct。

abstract.en: Direct is geometry turned into social life: a line becomes an order, a letter, a film, a career.
abstract.cn: direct 是几何变成社会生活：一条线变成命令、信件、影片、职业。

abstract.en: Every direct relation removes a middle term, whether a stop, an intermediary, or a detour in speech.
abstract.cn: 每一种直接关系都去掉一个中间项：无论是一个停靠点、一个中间人，还是言语中的绕路。

abstract.en: To direct is to choose one line and make others follow it; authority is the power to draw that line.
abstract.cn: 指导就是选一条线并让别人跟随；权威就是画这条线的权力。
