root: 拉丁语 dirigere“使直、引导”，由 dis-“分开”+ regere“保持笔直”构成；同族有 direction、director、regulate。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of direct, all built on one shape: a straight line. The line becomes a route, an aim, a chain of command, a form of address, a film, or an electric current.
sensesIntro.cn: direct 的九个义项都建立在一个形状上：直线。这条线可以是路线、瞄准、指挥链、称呼方式、影片，或电流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line with no bend and no detour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不弯、不绕的直线。

branches.en: STRAIGHT: no turn, no middle step, no reversal.
branches.cn: 直线：不拐弯、无中间环节、不反向。

branches.en: AIM: the line runs from a source to a target.
branches.cn: 瞄准：线从来源射向目标。

branches.en: GUIDE AND MANAGE: one person keeps others on the chosen line, whether a group or a production.
branches.cn: 引导与管理：一个人让别人保持在选定的线上，无论群体还是作品。

branches.en: ADDRESS: a message is aimed along a line at one recipient.
branches.cn: 称呼：信息沿一条线射向一个收件人。

branches.en: CANDID: speech with no detour, meaning travelling straight to the listener.
branches.cn: 直率：不绕路的言语，意思直线到达听者。

intro.en: Direct is both adjective and verb. English builds a large family with -ly, -ness, -ion, -or, -ory, and the negative or reversing prefixes in-, mis-, and re-.
intro.cn: direct 既是形容词也是动词。英语用 -ly、-ness、-ion、-or、-ory 以及否定或反向前缀 in-、mis-、re- 构成庞大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin dirigere 'set straight' gives directus 'straight' and director 'a guide'. The root regere also gives regime, regulate, and rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere“使直”生成 directus“直的”与 director“引导者”。词根 regere 还生成 regime、regulate、rule。

items.meaning: in a straight or immediate way
the quality of being straight or plain
the course in which something moves; also, guidance
relating to direction, as in a directional signal
an official instruction; also, instructing
a person who directs an organization, film, or project
a list of names, files, or places; originally a book of directions
items.example: look up the number in the directory

items.meaning: not straight; not immediate
to aim or guide wrongly
to send something in a new direction

definition_zh: 纪律；学科；训练；管教；惩罚
definition_en: training that produces order and self-control, a field of study, or the act of correcting someone
core_image: 一排笔直站立的士兵，脚下有一条看不见的准线
scene: 操场上，教官面对一队新兵，哨子挂在胸前。 On the parade ground the instructor trained a squad of new soldiers and stressed discipline again and again.
sceneCN: 这里 discipline 是「纪律」（第 2 个义项：使人服从的训练）；句意：操场上，教官训练一队新兵，反复强调纪律。

pos.zh: 纪律；自律；学科；训练；惩戒

senses.title: A system of rules
senses.definition: an organized set of rules that controls how an activity is done
senses.definitionCN: 控制某项活动如何进行的有组织规则
senses.example: The school's discipline is explained in the handbook.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的规章制度写在手册里。
senses.why: The mid-14c sense was 'system of rules and regulations'. Rules are the frame inside which instruction can happen, which is why discipline and teaching share one word.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中期的义项是“规章制度体系”。规则是教学得以发生的框架，所以 discipline 与 teaching 共用一个词。

senses.title: Training that produces obedience
senses.definition: training that teaches people to follow orders and act correctly
senses.definitionCN: 教人服从命令、正确行动的训练
senses.example: Recruits endure weeks of discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵要经受数周训练。
senses.why: The late 15c military sense grew from 'training to follow orders and act in accordance with rules'. The body is drilled until correct action becomes automatic.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪晚期的军事义来自“训练人服从命令、按规则行动”。身体被反复操练，直到正确动作成为本能。

senses.title: Self-control
senses.definition: the ability to control your own behavior and keep working
senses.definitionCN: 控制自身行为并坚持做事的能力
senses.example: It takes discipline to train daily.
senses.exampleCN: 每天训练需要自律。
senses.why: Around 1500 the sense 'orderly conduct as a result of training' appeared. When the rule is internalized, the one who obeys and the one who commands are the same person.
senses.whyCN: 约 1500 年出现“训练造成的井然有序行为”这一义项。当规则被内化，服从者与命令者就成了同一个人。

senses.title: Orderly conduct
senses.definition: behavior that shows training and respect for rules
senses.definitionCN: 显示受过训练并尊重规则的行为
senses.example: The troops showed great discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 部队表现出极强的纪律性。
senses.why: This is the outward face of the same sense: an observer sees order in the group. Discipline is both what is trained into a person and what others see coming out.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一义项的外在面：观察者看到群体中的秩序。discipline 既是被训练进人体的东西，也是别人看到它表现出来的样子。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: a branch of knowledge taught and researched in a university
senses.definitionCN: 大学中讲授与研究的某一知识分支
senses.example: History is a broad academic discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学是一门宽泛的学科。
senses.why: The late 14c sense 'branch of instruction or education' treats a subject as a body of teaching with its own rules and methods. A discipline is what can be discipled.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪晚期的“教学分支”义把一门科目看作有自身规则与方法的教学体系。一门 discipline 就是可以被人学习传承的东西。

senses.title: Punishment for correction
senses.definition: punishment intended to restore order rather than to harm
senses.definitionCN: 旨在恢复秩序而非造成伤害的惩罚
senses.example: The teacher used discipline, not abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师用的是惩戒，不是虐待。
senses.why: The earliest sense, c. 1200, was 'penitential chastisement; punishment for the sake of correction'. Correction is the purpose; pain is only the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 最早义（约 1200 年）是“忏悔性惩罚；为纠正而施罚”。纠正才是目的，痛苦只是工具。

senses.title: To train or control
senses.definition: to train a person or group to behave in an orderly way
senses.definitionCN: 训练一个人或群体有序行事
senses.example: Parents must discipline their children.
senses.exampleCN: 父母必须管教孩子。
senses.why: The verb, recorded c. 1300, first meant 'subject to discipline, correct, chastise', and by the late 14c 'instruct, educate, train'. Training and correction are two sides of the same act.
senses.whyCN: 动词最早记录于约 1300 年，义为“使受纪律、纠正、惩戒”，到 14 世纪晚期又指“教导、教育、训练”。训练与纠正是同一动作的两面。

senses.title: To punish officially
senses.definition: to impose an official penalty on someone for breaking rules
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则者施加正式处罚
senses.example: The committee disciplined two officers.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会处分了两名警官。
senses.why: The correction branch survives in institutions: a committee disciplines a member by applying the rule's penalty. The word keeps the moral frame of restoring order.
senses.whyCN: “纠正”分支在机构中保留下来：委员会通过施加规则处罚来 discipline 成员。这个词仍保留恢复秩序的道德框架。

senses.title: Church law and practice
senses.definition: the system of rules and practices regulating a church
senses.definitionCN: 规范教会行为的规则与修行体系
senses.example: The monks followed a strict discipline.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们遵循严格的修行制度。
senses.why: The 1570s sense was 'the system by which the practice of a church is regulated'. Here discipline is almost pure rule: a way of life laid down for a community.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 70 年代的义项是“规范教会实践的体系”。这里的 discipline 几乎是纯粹的规则：为群体规定的一种生活方式。

intro.en: Discipline began as correction and became both a field of study and a way of life. Its base, discipulus 'pupil', has an origin that scholars still dispute.
intro.cn: discipline 从“纠正”开始，后来同时成为学科与生活方式。它的词基 discipulus“学生”的来源，学者至今仍有争议。

items.en: The noun means 'penitential chastisement; punishment for the sake of correction'.
items.cn: 名词义为“忏悔性惩罚；为纠正而施罚”。

items.en: descepline meant 'discipline, physical punishment; teaching; suffering; martyrdom'.
items.cn: descepline 意为“纪律、体罚；教学；受苦；殉道”。

items.en: disciplina 'instruction given, teaching, learning, knowledge', from discipulus 'pupil, student, follower'.
items.cn: disciplina 意为“所授的教导、教学、学习、知识”，来自 discipulus“学生、追随者”。

items.en: discipulus is of uncertain origin. OED and Watkins suggest discere 'to learn'; Barnhart and Klein suggest a lost *discipere 'grasp intellectually'; de Vaan finds both explanations weak. The etymology is therefore uncertain, and no single proposal is adopted here.
items.cn: discipulus 的来源不确定。OED 与 Watkins 认为来自 discere“学习”；Barnhart 与 Klein 认为来自已失传的 *discipere“理智地把握”；de Vaan 认为两说都缺乏说服力。词源存疑，本文不强行选定一说。

items.en: 'System of rules and regulations' appears; by late 14c, 'branch of instruction or education'.
items.cn: “规章制度体系”义出现；到 14 世纪晚期又有“教学分支”义。

items.en: 'Military training' is late 15c.; 'orderly conduct as a result of training' is c. 1500; church discipline is from the 1570s.
items.cn: “军事训练”义在 15 世纪晚期；“训练造成的井然有序行为”约 1500 年；教会 discipline 义始于 16 世纪 70 年代。

note.en: The first group is about the discipline word family and its closest look-alikes; the second is about words that also mean training, order, or a subject.
note.cn: 第一组看 discipline 词族与最相近的形近词，第二组看同样表示训练、秩序或学科的词。

entries.definition: a pupil or follower, especially of a teacher or religious leader. It is the base noun behind discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 学生、追随者，尤指某教师或宗教领袖的门徒。它是 discipline 背后的基础名词。

entries.definition: a person who insists on strict discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 严格执行纪律的人。

entries.definition: trained to behave in an orderly, controlled way.
entries.definitionCN: 有纪律的；训练有素的。

entries.definition: organized practice to develop a skill. It is the activity; discipline is the order that training produces.
entries.definitionCN: 为培养技能而进行的有组织练习。它是活动，discipline 是训练产生的秩序。

entries.definition: a condition in which everything is in its proper place or follows rules. It is the result discipline aims at.
entries.definitionCN: 一切各就各位、依规则运行的状态。它是 discipline 追求的结果。

entries.definition: an area of study or work. It is close to the academic sense of discipline but less tied to a method.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或工作的领域。它接近 discipline 的学科义，但较少强调方法。

entries.definition: a penalty imposed for wrongdoing. Discipline may use punishment, but its purpose is correction.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错施加的处罚。discipline 可以使用惩罚，但目的是纠正。

normalIntro.en: Real links: discipulus 'pupil', disciplina 'teaching', the military sense, self-discipline, and church discipline.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：discipulus“学生”、disciplina“教学”、军事义、自律，以及教会 discipline。

normal.en: The base is discipulus, 'pupil'. A discipline is what a pupil is taught, and also the order that teaching installs.
normal.cn: 词基是 discipulus“学生”。discipline 既是学生所学的内容，也是教学建立的秩序。

normal.en: Early discipline was correction, not cruelty: punishment for the sake of setting something right.
normal.cn: 早期的 discipline 是纠正，不是残酷：为把事情摆正而施罚。

normal.en: Military training made the word physical: repeated drill until obedience becomes automatic.
normal.cn: 军事训练让这个词变得身体化：反复操练，直到服从成为本能。

normal.en: Self-discipline is the same rule turned inward; the commander and the obeyed are one person.
normal.cn: 自律是同一条规则转向内部；发令者与服从者成了同一个人。

normal.en: An academic discipline is a field with its own rules of evidence and method, a community of pupils and teachers.
normal.cn: 一门学科是一个有自身证据与方法规则的领域，一个师生共同体。

abstract.en: Discipline is order made durable: it does not remove disorder once, it builds a shape that resists disorder.
abstract.cn: 纪律是变得持久的秩序：它不是一次性消除混乱，而是造出一个能抵抗混乱的形状。

abstract.en: The word joins two opposite experiences, being taught and being punished, because both aim at the same corrected form.
abstract.cn: 这个词连接了两种相反的经验——被教导与被惩罚——因为两者都朝向同一个被纠正的形状。

abstract.en: A discipline is also a boundary: it decides which questions belong inside and which methods count as valid.
abstract.cn: 一门学科也是一条边界：它决定哪些问题属于内部、哪些方法算有效。

examples.en: Good discipline is built on clear routines.
examples.cn: 好的纪律建立在清晰的日常规范上。

examples.en: History is a broad academic discipline.
examples.cn: 历史学是一门宽泛的学科。

examples.en: Parents must discipline their children with care.
examples.cn: 父母必须用心管教孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: “弟子扑棱”——弟子扑棱着站齐 → discipline 纪律、训练

root: 拉丁语 disciplina“教导、学问”，来自 discipulus“学生”；discipulus 的词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of discipline, all built on one relation: a rule that shapes a person. The rule can be external (order, punishment, church law) or internal (self-control), and the shaped person can become a member of a field.
sensesIntro.cn: discipline 的九个义项都建立在一个关系上：塑造人的规则。规则可以是外在的（秩序、惩罚、教会法规），也可以是内在的（自律），被塑造的人还可以成为一个领域的成员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on the ground that a row of soldiers stands along.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面上一条让一队士兵站齐的准线。

branches.en: ORDER: rules produce visible order, and order becomes a personal habit.
branches.cn: 秩序：规则产生可见秩序，秩序又变成个人习惯。

branches.en: TRAIN AND CORRECT: drill and punishment are two instruments for shaping behavior.
branches.cn: 训练与纠正：操练与惩罚是塑造行为的两种工具。

branches.en: FIELD: a body of teaching with its own rules becomes an academic discipline.
branches.cn: 学科：拥有自身规则的教学体系成为一门学科。

branches.en: PUNISHMENT: correction is the purpose, pain only the instrument.
branches.cn: 惩罚：纠正才是目的，痛苦只是工具。

branches.en: CHURCH: a whole community's way of life is regulated as discipline.
branches.cn: 教会：整个群体的生活方式被作为 discipline 规范。

intro.en: Discipline is both noun and verb. English adds -ed, -ary, -arian, -able, and the prefixes self-, multi-, inter-, and in- to build the family.
intro.cn: discipline 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ed、-ary、-arian、-able，以及前缀 self-、multi-、inter-、in- 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin disciplina and discipulus share a root that is disputed. Related English words keep the 'learning' idea; the etymological link to discere 'learn' is plausible but not proven.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 disciplina 与 discipulus 共享一个有争议的词根。相关英语词保留“学习”之意；与 discere“学习”的词源联系虽有可能，但未获证实。

items.meaning: trained to behave in an orderly, controlled way
relating to discipline or punishment
a person who enforces strict discipline
able or willing to be taught and corrected
lacking order or self-control
items.meaningCN: 缺乏纪律的（un- 表否定）

items.meaning: the ability to control oneself without outside enforcement
combining several academic disciplines
crossing the boundaries between disciplines
lack of discipline

latinEntries.meaningCN: 学习（与 discipulus 的关系为通行推测，未证实）

definition_en: to make something known or visible that was hidden or closed
core_image: 一封封好的信被拆开，里面的字露出来
scene: 记者追问下，公司代表面前摆着那份合同。 Under the reporter's questioning, the company finally disclosed the terms of the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 disclose 是「透露、公开」（第 1 个义项：揭示秘密信息）；句意：在记者的追问下，公司终于公开了合同的条款。

senses.title: Reveal secret information
senses.definition: to make hidden information known to others
senses.definitionCN: 让隐藏的信息为他人所知
senses.example: The company disclosed the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司披露了合同条款。
senses.why: The word is literally 'un-close': Old French desclore opens what was shut. A sealed document is the model, so revealing information is pictured as opening a container.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上是“打开封闭”：古法语 desclore 打开原本关着的东西。密封文件是原型，因此“透露信息”被想象成打开容器。

senses.title: Make something visible
senses.definition: to allow something previously unseen to be seen
senses.definitionCN: 让先前看不见的东西被看见
senses.example: The scan disclosed a small fracture.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示了一处小骨折。
senses.why: A scan opens the body to view the way a door opens a room. The medical use keeps the original optical sense: what was closed is now exposed to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 扫描像开门一样把身体打开给人看。医学用法保留了最初的光学义：原本闭合的东西现在暴露在眼前。

senses.title: Open something physically closed
senses.titleCN: 打开物理上封闭之物（古义）
senses.definition: in older use, to open a sealed letter or container
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，打开密封的信件或容器
senses.example: The letter was disclosed with a knife.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信是用刀拆开的。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal layer: desclore meant 'open, break open, unlock'. The modern information sense is a metaphor drawn from this physical opening.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面层：desclore 意为“打开、破开、解锁”。现代的信息义正是从这个物理打开动作借来的隐喻。

senses.title: Reveal documents by legal duty
senses.definition: to release records that a law or regulator requires to be made public
senses.definitionCN: 公开法律或监管机构要求公开的记录
senses.example: The bank must disclose its records to regulators.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须向监管机构披露记录。
senses.why: Law borrows the word's completeness: disclosure must open the whole record, not a selected part. The duty turns a physical opening into an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了这个词的“完整”意味：披露必须打开整份记录，而不是挑选的一部分。义务把物理打开变成法律责任。

senses.title: Reveal a feeling unintentionally
senses.definition: to show a feeling or fact without meaning to
senses.definitionCN: 无意间表现出情绪或事实
senses.example: His smile disclosed his relief.
senses.exampleCN: 他的微笑流露出松了一口气。
senses.why: When the opening is not deliberate, the body becomes the unsealed letter. The word can name a leak of meaning that the person did not choose to release.
senses.whyCN: 当打开并非有意，身体就成了被拆开的信。这个词可以指人并未选择释放、却漏出的意义。

senses.title: Publish financial information
senses.definition: to report financial facts as required by market rules
senses.definitionCN: 按市场规则报告财务事实
senses.example: Companies disclose earnings quarterly.
senses.exampleCN: 公司每季度披露收益。
senses.why: Investors need the closed books opened at fixed intervals. Disclosure here is a routine, scheduled opening rather than a dramatic revelation.
senses.whyCN: 投资者需要账本在固定时点被打开。这里的 disclose 是例行、按时的打开，而非戏剧性的揭露。

senses.title: Expose to view, as a stage
senses.definition: to reveal a scene by removing a covering
senses.definitionCN: 通过移开遮蔽物显出景象
senses.example: The curtain rose and disclosed the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起，露出舞台。
senses.why: A curtain is a cover; raising it un-closes the view. This sense keeps the spatial image almost intact, with no information involved, only visibility.
senses.whyCN: 幕布是遮盖物；把它升起就是“打开”视野。这个义项几乎完整保留空间意象，不涉及信息，只涉及可见性。

senses.title: Name a source or identity
senses.definition: to reveal who provided information or who someone is
senses.definitionCN: 揭示信息提供者或某人的身份
senses.example: He refused to disclose the source.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝透露消息来源。
senses.why: Journalism treats a source as a protected closed box. To disclose is to open that box, which is why the verb carries both transparency and risk.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业把消息来源当作受保护的封闭盒子。disclose 就是打开这个盒子，因此这个词同时带有透明与风险。

intro.en: Disclose is built from a negative prefix plus 'close': to disclose is literally to un-close. The physical image of opening a sealed thing still sits under every modern use.
intro.cn: disclose 由否定前缀加“关闭”构成：字面上就是“打开封闭”。打开密封之物的物理意象，仍位于每一个现代用法之下。

items.en: disclosen 'to uncover and expose to view, open to the knowledge of others'.
items.cn: disclosen 义为“揭开并显露于视野，向他人公开知识”。

items.en: From desclos, past participle of desclore 'open, break open, unlock, reveal'.
items.cn: 来自 desclos，即 desclore“打开、破开、解锁、揭示”的过去分词。

items.en: des- 'opposite of' + clore 'to close', from Latin claudere 'to shut, close, block up'.
items.cn: des-“相反”+ clore“关闭”，来自拉丁语 claudere“关、闭、堵住”。

items.en: claudere is linked to PIE *klau- 'hook, peg, nail', the things used as locks or bolts in primitive structures.
items.cn: claudere 与原始印欧语 *klau-“钩、钉、销”有关，这些正是原始结构里用作锁或门闩的东西。

items.en: The noun disclosure, 'act of opening up to view, making known', is formed in English, perhaps on the model of closure.
items.cn: 名词 disclosure“打开给人看、使人知道的行为”在英语中形成，可能仿 closure 造出。

note.en: The first group is about close and its family, which share the same root; the second is about verbs that also make hidden things known.
note.cn: 第一组看 close 及其同根词族，第二组看同样让隐藏之事为人所知的动词。

entries.definition: to shut something. Disclose adds the negative prefix des-, so the two are mirror images.
entries.definitionCN: 关上某物。disclose 加了否定前缀 des-，两者是镜像。

entries.definition: the act of closing something, or a sense of finality.
entries.definitionCN: 关闭的行为；也指一种了结感。

entries.definition: not revealed; kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 未披露的；保密的。

entries.definition: to make something hidden known, often something significant. It is more dramatic than disclose.
entries.definitionCN: 使隐藏之事为人所知，常指重要之事。它比 disclose 更戏剧化。

entries.definition: to reveal secret or private information, often reluctantly. It is narrower and more confidential than disclose.
entries.definitionCN: 泄露秘密或私人信息，常含不情愿。它比 disclose 更窄、更机密。

entries.definition: to leave something uncovered or make wrongdoing public. It stresses vulnerability rather than information.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物暴露，或公开不法行为。它强调脆弱性，而非信息。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the des- + close structure, the sealed letter image, legal disclosure, and the noun disclosure.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：des- + close 的结构、密封信的意象、法律披露，以及名词 disclosure。

normal.en: Disclose = dis- 'opposite' + close. The word is a mirror: to disclose is to un-close.
normal.cn: disclose = dis-“相反”+ close。这个词是一面镜子：disclose 就是“不关闭”。

normal.en: The original picture is a sealed letter opened with a knife: the contents come into view.
normal.cn: 最初的画面是用刀拆开密封的信：内容进入视野。

normal.en: A scan discloses a fracture in the same way a door discloses a room.
normal.cn: 扫描显示骨折，就像开门让房间显露一样。

normal.en: Legal disclosure must open the whole record, not a chosen page.
normal.cn: 法律上的披露必须打开整份记录，而不是挑一页。

normal.en: A smile can disclose a feeling the person never chose to reveal.
normal.cn: 一个微笑可以泄露当事人并不打算表露的情绪。

abstract.en: Disclosure is controlled visibility: someone decides which closed thing is opened, and for whom.
abstract.cn: 披露是受控的可见性：某人决定打开哪个封闭之物，以及给谁看。

abstract.en: The same word covers transparency and leakage, because both remove a cover; ethics lies in who chose the opening.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖透明与泄漏，因为两者都移除了遮盖；伦理在于是谁选择了打开。

abstract.en: Every secret is a closed container, and every act of knowledge is a small act of un-closing.
abstract.cn: 每个秘密都是一个封闭容器，每一次获知都是一次小小的“打开”。

examples.en: The company disclosed the terms of the contract.
examples.cn: 公司披露了合同条款。

examples.en: The scan disclosed a small fracture.
examples.cn: 扫描显示了一处小骨折。

examples.en: He refused to disclose the source.
examples.cn: 他拒绝透露消息来源。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地司楼”——把地司楼的门打开给人看 → disclose 揭露、透露

root: 古法语 desclore“打开、解锁”，由 des-“相反”+ clore“关闭”构成；拉丁语 claudere“关闭”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of disclose, all built on one act: removing a cover. The cover can be a seal, a curtain, a legal duty, or a person's face, and what comes out can be information or simply visibility.
sensesIntro.cn: disclose 的八个义项都建立在一个动作上：移开遮盖。遮盖可以是封印、幕布、法律责任或人的表情，露出的可以是信息，也可以只是可见性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter opened, its contents exposed to view.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封密封的信被拆开，内容暴露在视野中。

branches.en: PERSONAL SECRET: a hidden fact, a source, or an identity is opened to the listener.
branches.cn: 个人秘密：隐藏的事实、来源或身份向听者打开。

branches.en: DUTY AND MARKET: law forces documents open, and companies open their finances to investors.
branches.cn: 义务与市场：法律迫使文件公开，公司向投资者公开财务。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: the open thing is exposed to the eye, with no information claim.
branches.cn: 可见性：被打开之物暴露于眼前，不涉及信息主张。

branches.en: LITERAL: the oldest layer is a physical letter or container being opened.
branches.cn: 字面：最古老层是物理信件或容器被打开。

branches.en: INVOLUNTARY: a face or gesture opens without the person choosing it.
branches.cn: 非自愿：表情或手势未经选择地打开。

intro.en: Disclose is a verb; English adds -ure, -ed, -ing, -er, and the negative prefix un-, plus self- and non- compounds.
intro.cn: disclose 是动词；英语加 -ure、-ed、-ing、-er，以及否定前缀 un-，还有 self-、non- 复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere 'to close' also gives clause, claustrophobia, and conclude. Disclose reverses it with des-, the Old French form of dis-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claudere“关闭”还生成 clause、claustrophobia、conclude。disclose 用古法语 des-（即 dis-）把它反转。

items.meaning: the act of making something known; the fact revealed
items.meaningCN: 披露；被揭露的事实（-ure 构成名词）

items.meaning: made known or visible
not revealed
the act of revealing; also an adjective
a person who discloses something
the act of revealing personal information about oneself
failure or refusal to disclose, often bound by an agreement
items.meaningCN: 不披露（non- 表否定；常指保密协议）

items.meaning: the practice of making all relevant information public

latinEntries.meaning: a bolt, bar; an enclosed place

definition_zh: 区分；辨别；歧视；区别对待
definition_en: to perceive a difference between things, or to treat people unequally because of their group
core_image: 用筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开
scene: 招聘会上，面试官翻着一份简历，年龄栏被红笔圈起。 At the job fair the interviewer discriminated against an applicant because of her age.
sceneCN: 这里 discriminate 是「歧视」（第 4 个义项：因群体身份而不公平对待）；句意：招聘会上，面试官因为年龄而歧视一位应聘者。

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 区分开

senses.title: Perceive a difference
senses.definition: to notice that two things are different
senses.definitionCN: 注意到两件事物不同
senses.example: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。
senses.why: Latin discriminare means 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'distinction'. The first English sense, 1620s, is the mental act of marking that division.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 discriminare 意为“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”。英语最早义（17 世纪 20 年代）就是在心里标记这条分界。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.titleCN: 把一物与另一物区分开
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between two specific things
senses.definitionCN: 认出两个具体事物之间的差异
senses.example: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。
senses.why: The verb takes two objects because the line is drawn between them. discrimen is the interval or mark between two things, so discrimination is always relational.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词带两个宾语，因为线是在两者之间画的。discrimen 就是两物之间的间隔或标记，所以“区分”总是关系性的。

senses.title: Show fine judgment or taste
senses.definition: to show the ability to make careful distinctions, especially in quality
senses.definitionCN: 表现出仔细辨别、尤指辨别品质的能力
senses.example: She has a discriminating palate for wine.
senses.exampleCN: 她对葡萄酒有敏锐的鉴别力。
senses.why: The adjective discriminating (1792) is the positive side of the same skill. A person who can sift fine differences is said to have taste, not prejudice.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 discriminating（1792）是同一能力的正面面。能筛出细微差异的人被说成品味好，而不是有偏见。

senses.title: Treat people unequally
senses.definition: to treat people differently and unfairly because of their group
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体而不公平地对待人
senses.example: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
senses.exampleCN: 因年龄歧视是违法的。
senses.why: The adverse sense, 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons', is first recorded in 1866 in American English. The neutral line-drawing turns into a hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于 1866 年的美国英语。中性的画线变成了等级。

senses.title: Discriminate against someone
senses.definition: to deny someone opportunities or fair treatment because of who they are
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的身份而剥夺机会或公平待遇
senses.example: The firm was accused of discriminating against women.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被指控歧视女性。
senses.why: The fixed pattern discriminate against makes the target explicit. The verb now names an action with a victim, not merely a perception.
senses.whyCN: 固定搭配 discriminate against 明确点出受害者。这个动词现在指带有受害者的行为，而不只是感知。

senses.title: Separate signals from noise
senses.definition: in electronics, to select wanted signals and reject unwanted ones
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中选出所需信号、排除干扰
senses.example: The circuit discriminates noise from signal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个电路能鉴别噪声与信号。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the original 'sift' image almost literally: a circuit separates one kind of input from another and passes only the wanted kind.
senses.whyCN: 工程学几乎字面保留了“筛”的意象：电路把一类输入与另一类分开，只放行所需的一类。

senses.title: Apply a discriminatory rule
senses.definition: to operate a rule or practice that disadvantages a protected group
senses.definitionCN: 执行使受保护群体处于不利地位的规则或做法
senses.example: Landlords may not discriminate against tenants with children.
senses.exampleCN: 房东不得歧视带孩子的租户。
senses.why: Legal usage turns the verb into a name for a prohibited practice. The distinction is no longer neutral; the law defines which lines may not be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把这个动词变成对禁止行为的称呼。区分不再中性；法律界定哪些线不得画。

senses.title: Distinct, marked off (archaic adjective)
senses.titleCN: 独特的；被区分开的（古形容词）
senses.definition: in 17c. use, an adjective meaning 'distinct'
senses.definitionCN: 在 17 世纪用法中作形容词，意为“独特的”
senses.example: In 17c. texts a discriminate difference meant a clearly marked one.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪文本中，a discriminate difference 指被清楚标出的差异。
senses.why: The adjective sense, recorded 1620s, meant 'distinct'; the later sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798. It survives mainly inside discriminating and indiscriminate.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“独特的”；后来“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。它主要残留在 discriminating 与 indiscriminate 中。

intro.en: Discriminate began as a neutral act of separating, then acquired one of the strongest social meanings in English. The root cernere 'to sift' explains both the neutral and the contested senses.
intro.cn: discriminate 起初是中性的“分开”动作，后来获得英语中最强烈的社会含义之一。词根 cernere“筛”解释了它的中性义与争议义。

items.en: The verb means 'distinguish from something else or from each other, observe or mark the differences'.
items.cn: 动词义为“把某物与别物区分开，或观察并标记差异”。

items.en: From discriminatus, past participle of discriminare 'to divide, separate', from discrimen 'interval, distinction'.
items.cn: 来自 discriminatus，即 discriminare“分开、分离”的过去分词，源头是 discrimen“间隔、区别”。

items.en: discrimen derives from discernere 'to separate, sift, distinguish', from dis- 'off, away' + cernere 'sift' (PIE *krei- 'to sieve').
items.cn: discrimen 来自 discernere“分开、筛、辨别”，由 dis-“离开”+ cernere“筛”（原始印欧语 *krei-“筛”）。

items.en: An adjective sense 'distinct' is recorded; the sense 'perceiving nice differences' is from 1798.
items.cn: 形容词义“独特的”被记录；“能察觉细微差异”的义项始于 1798 年。

items.en: discriminating 'possessing discernment' appears, the positive side of the same skill.
items.cn: discriminating“有辨别力的”出现，是同一能力的正面面。

items.en: The adverse sense 'make invidious distinctions prejudicial to a class of persons' is first recorded in American English.
items.cn: 负面义“对某类人作出有害区分”最早记录于美国英语。

note.en: The first group is about forms in the same family; the second is about verbs that also tell things apart.
note.cn: 第一组看同一词族的形态，第二组看同样把事物区分开的动词。

entries.definition: showing careful judgment and good taste; the positive sense of the skill.
entries.definitionCN: 有鉴别力的；品味好的（该能力的正面义）。

entries.definition: unfairly treating a group; the negative institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 歧视性的；不公平对待群体的（负面的制度义）。

entries.definition: done without choosing carefully; random or widespread.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区分的；随意的（in- 表否定）。

entries.definition: to see or show a difference, often with careful attention. It is neutral and broad.
entries.definitionCN: 看出或表明差异，常含仔细留意。它中性而宽泛。

entries.definition: to make or recognize a difference, especially in a technical or systematic way.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同或认出差异，尤指技术性、系统性地。

entries.definition: to perceive something with difficulty or subtlety. It stresses the effort of seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 费力或细微地察觉某物。它强调“看见”的努力。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the root cernere 'sift', the 1866 social sense, the positive discriminating, and the legal pattern discriminate against.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：词根 cernere“筛”、1866 年的社会义、正面的 discriminating，以及法律搭配 discriminate against。

normal.en: The root cernere means 'to sift'. To discriminate is to pass things through a sieve and keep the wanted grains.
normal.cn: 词根 cernere 意为“筛”。discriminate 就是把东西过筛，留下想要的颗粒。

normal.en: discrimen is the interval between two things; a distinction exists only where two items meet.
normal.cn: discrimen 是两物之间的间隔；只有两物相遇之处才有区分。

normal.en: discriminating taste is the same sieve used well: fine differences are kept, coarse ones rejected.
normal.cn: discriminating taste 就是使用得当的同一张筛子：留下细微差异，筛掉粗糙之处。

normal.en: In 1866 American English the neutral sieve became a hierarchy: some people were sorted out and denied fair treatment.
normal.cn: 1866 年美国英语中，中性的筛子变成了等级：一些人被筛出去，失去公平待遇。

normal.en: The legal pattern discriminate against names a victim, which is why it is the strongest use of the word.
normal.cn: 法律搭配 discriminate against 点明受害者，因此是这个词语气最强的用法。

abstract.en: Discrimination is selection: every sieve includes and excludes at once. The ethics lie in who chose the mesh.
abstract.cn: 区分就是选择：每张筛子都同时容纳与排除。伦理在于是谁选了筛孔。

abstract.en: The word holds both discernment and prejudice because both are acts of sorting; only the purpose separates them.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时容纳“鉴别力”与“偏见”，因为两者都是分拣动作；区分它们的是目的。

abstract.en: A just distinction marks differences without using them to deny a share; an unjust one turns a difference into a rank.
abstract.cn: 公正的区分标出差异却不借此剥夺份额；不公正的区分把差异变成等级。

examples.en: Babies can discriminate between familiar and new faces.
examples.cn: 婴儿能分辨熟悉与陌生的面孔。

examples.en: It is illegal to discriminate by age.
examples.cn: 因年龄歧视是违法的。

examples.en: Readers must discriminate fact from opinion.
examples.cn: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地是亏米”——地里的米亏了，要筛一筛分开好坏 → discriminate 区分、歧视

root: 拉丁语 discriminare“分开、分离”，来自 discrimen“区别”，再上为 discernere“筛、辨别”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of discriminate, all built on one act: sifting. Sifting can be neutral (telling kinds apart), skilled (good taste), technical (separating signal from noise), or unjust (denying a group fair treatment).
sensesIntro.cn: discriminate 的八个义项都建立在一个动作上：筛。筛可以是中性的（分出种类）、有技巧的（好品味）、技术的（分离信号与噪声），或是不义的（剥夺某群体的公平待遇）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve separating grains of different sizes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张筛子把大小不同的颗粒分开。

branches.en: SEPARATE: the neutral core, drawing a line between two kinds and telling them apart.
branches.cn: 分开：中性核心，在两类之间画线并把它们辨开。

branches.en: MARKED OFF: the old adjective describes the thing that has been separated and stands distinct.
branches.cn: 被标出：旧形容词描述已被分开、独自成立之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: the same sieve used with skill produces discriminating taste.
branches.cn: 品质：同一张筛子用得娴熟，就产生有鉴别力的品味。

branches.en: PREJUDICE: the line becomes a hierarchy and denies fair treatment.
branches.cn: 偏见：线变成等级，剥夺公平待遇。

branches.en: SIGNAL: engineering keeps the literal sieve, passing one kind of input only.
branches.cn: 信号：工程学保留字面的筛，只放行一类输入。

intro.en: Discriminate is built on the Latin stem discrimin-. English adds -tion, -tory, -ting, -tive, -able, and the negative prefixes in- and non-.
intro.cn: discriminate 建立在拉丁词干 discrimin- 上。英语加 -tion、-tory、-ting、-tive、-able，以及否定前缀 in-、non-。

latinIntro.en: Latin discriminare, discrimen, and discernere all belong to the 'sift' family. Cernere 'to sift' also underlies discern, secret, and certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discriminare、discrimen、discernere 都属于“筛”的词族。cernere“筛”也是 discern、secret、certain 的深层来源。

items.meaning: the act of distinguishing; also, unfair treatment of a group
items.meaningCN: 区分；歧视（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: treating a group unfairly
showing careful judgment and fine taste
serving to distinguish or select
able to be distinguished
done without careful selection; random
not treating any group unfairly
having been distinguished or treated unfairly
opposing unfair treatment of groups

definition_en: to talk or write about a subject in detail, often to exchange ideas or reach a decision
core_image: 一群人围桌把一个问题摊开来逐块敲碎
scene: 会议室里，团队围着预算表和白板。 In the meeting room the team discussed next quarter's budget around the table.
sceneCN: 这里 discuss 是「讨论」（第 1 个义项：就某话题交谈）；句意：会议室里，团队围桌讨论下季度的预算。

senses.title: Talk over a topic
senses.definition: to exchange ideas about a subject with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人就某主题交换看法
senses.example: We discussed the plan for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们讨论了这个计划一个小时。
senses.why: Latin discutere meant 'dash to pieces, shake apart'. By the 15c the mental image became 'examine from every side', which is exactly what a good discussion does to a topic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 discutere 意为“打碎、摇散”。到 15 世纪，心智意象变成“从各方面检视”，这正是好的讨论对话题所做的事。

senses.title: Debate formally
senses.definition: to argue the merits of a proposal in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合辩论某提案的优劣
senses.example: The committee discussed the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会讨论了这项法案。
senses.why: The mid-15c sense 'examine by argument, debate' is the usual modern sense. Discussion separates a proposal into its parts, the way discutere once broke things apart.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期义“通过论证来检视、辩论”是通常的现代义。讨论把提案拆成部分，正如 discutere 曾把东西打碎。

senses.title: Treat a subject in writing
senses.definition: to examine a subject in a book, article, or speech
senses.definitionCN: 在书、文章或演讲中探讨某主题
senses.example: The chapter discusses three theories.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章论述了三种理论。
senses.why: A written discussion can last for pages without a live interlocutor. The word extends from spoken exchange to the orderly examination of a subject in text.
senses.whyCN: 书面讨论可以持续数页而没有现场对话者。这个词从口头交流扩展到文本中有条理的主题检视。

senses.title: Reach a decision by talking
senses.definition: to talk until a choice becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: 谈到作出选择
senses.example: They discussed whether to move.
senses.exampleCN: 他们商议是否搬家。
senses.why: Discussion is often instrumental: it shakes the options apart so that one can be chosen. The Latin 'shake apart' survives in this decision-making use.
senses.whyCN: 讨论常是工具性的：它把选项摇散，以便选出其一。拉丁语“摇散”在这一决策用法中仍然存在。

senses.title: Converse about something
senses.definition: to talk about something in a less formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在较非正式场合谈论某事
senses.example: Let's discuss it over lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 我们午饭时聊这件事吧。
senses.why: The word can shrink to ordinary conversation. The scale changes, but the shape remains: two or more people turning a subject over together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缩小为日常交谈。规模变了，形状不变：两个或更多人一起翻动一个话题。

senses.title: Review a case clinically
senses.definition: in medicine, to review a patient's case with colleagues
senses.definitionCN: 医学中与同事一起复核病人情况
senses.example: The team discussed the patient's scans.
senses.exampleCN: 团队讨论了病人的扫描结果。
senses.why: Clinical discussion is a formal examination of evidence among specialists. The subject is a case, and the goal is a shared judgment rather than a casual chat.
senses.whyCN: 临床讨论是专家之间对证据的正式检视。对象是一个病例，目标是共同判断，而非闲聊。

senses.title: Negotiate terms
senses.definition: to talk through the conditions of an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 逐条谈妥协议条件
senses.example: We are discussing terms with the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 我们正在与供应商商谈条件。
senses.why: When the subject is terms, discussion becomes bargaining. Each clause is examined and shaken until both sides accept a formulation.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是条款时，讨论变成议价。每条条款都被检视、摇动，直到双方接受一种表述。

senses.title: Hold a classroom discussion
senses.definition: to examine a topic together in class
senses.definitionCN: 在课堂上共同探讨一个主题
senses.example: The class discussed the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 全班讨论了这首诗。
senses.why: The educational sense applies the same structure to learning: students turn the text over together, guided by a teacher, and meaning is produced in the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 教育义把同一结构用于学习：学生在教师引导下共同翻动文本，意义在交流中产生。

intro.en: Discuss looks like 'talk', but its Latin body means 'shake apart'. The journey from smashing to examining explains why a discussion is supposed to break a question into pieces.
intro.cn: discuss 看起来是“谈话”，但它的拉丁语身体意为“摇散”。从打碎到检视的旅程，解释了为什么讨论应当把问题拆成碎片。

items.en: discussen 'to examine, investigate' is recorded.
items.cn: 记录到 discussen，义为“审查、调查”。

items.en: From discuss-, past participle stem of discutere 'to dash to pieces, agitate, strike or shake apart'.
items.cn: 来自 discutere 的分词词干 discuss-，意为“打成碎片、摇动、击散”。

items.en: discutere = dis- 'apart' + quatere 'to shake'. The same quatere underlies quash and concussion.
items.cn: discutere = dis-“分开”+ quatere“摇”。同一个 quatere 也是 quash 与 concussion 的来源。

items.en: In Late and Medieval Latin discutere also meant 'to discuss, examine, investigate'.
items.cn: 在晚期与中世纪拉丁语中，discutere 也指“讨论、审查、调查”。

items.en: The modern sense 'examine by argument, debate' appears (implied in discussing).
items.cn: 现代义“通过论证检视、辩论”出现（见于 discussing）。

note.en: The first group is about discus and the discuss family; the second is about verbs that also exchange views.
note.cn: 第一组看 discus 与 discuss 词族，第二组看同样交换看法的动词。

entries.definition: a heavy disc thrown in athletics. It comes from Greek diskos, not from discutere.
entries.definitionCN: 田径中投掷的重圆盘。它来自希腊语 diskos，与 discutere 无关。

entries.definition: the noun from discuss: an exchange of views or a written treatment.
entries.definitionCN: discuss 的名词：意见交流或书面论述。

entries.definition: the past tense and past participle of discuss.
entries.definitionCN: discuss 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: a formal argument in which opposing sides speak. It is more adversarial than discuss.
entries.definitionCN: 正反双方发言的正式辩论。它比 discuss 更具对抗性。

entries.definition: to discuss something informally before deciding. It is the everyday phrase for the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前非正式地讨论。它是同一动作的日常说法。

entries.definition: to discuss carefully in order to decide. It stresses the weighing of reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 为决定而仔细讨论。它强调权衡理由。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Latin discutere 'shake apart', the 15c shift to 'debate', and the many settings of discussion.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 discutere“摇散”、15 世纪转向“辩论”，以及讨论的多种场景。

normal.en: discutere is dis- 'apart' plus quatere 'shake': a discussion shakes a question until its parts separate.
normal.cn: discutere 是 dis-“分开”+ quatere“摇”：讨论把问题摇到各部分分开。

normal.en: The Latin word first meant 'smash to pieces'; Late Latin softened it into 'examine'. Breaking and examining share a method.
normal.cn: 拉丁词最初意为“打碎”；晚期拉丁语把它软化为“审查”。打碎与审查共享一种方法。

normal.en: In the mid-15c the usual sense became 'examine by argument, debate'.
normal.cn: 15 世纪中期，通常义变成“通过论证检视、辩论”。

normal.en: A chapter can discuss a theory with no one talking; the examination happens in writing.
normal.cn: 一章可以讨论一种理论而无人说话；检视发生在文字中。

normal.en: Medical and legal discussions are formal case reviews: specialists shake the evidence together.
normal.cn: 医学与法律讨论是正式的案件复核：专家一起摇动证据。

abstract.en: Discussion is analysis in company: the topic is divided, distributed, and reassembled as shared understanding.
abstract.cn: 讨论是集体分析：话题被拆分、分发，再作为共同理解重新组装。

abstract.en: The word's violent root is a reminder that real discussion disturbs a question; polite agreement may leave it unexamined.
abstract.cn: 这个词暴力的词根提醒人：真正的讨论会扰动问题；礼貌的附和可能让问题未被检视。

abstract.en: Every discussion draws a boundary around what counts as relevant, and that boundary is itself part of the outcome.
abstract.cn: 每次讨论都围绕“什么算相关”画一条边界，而这条边界本身就是结果的一部分。

examples.en: We discussed the plan for an hour.
examples.cn: 我们讨论了这个计划一个小时。

examples.en: The chapter discusses three theories.
examples.cn: 这一章论述了三种理论。

examples.en: The team discussed the patient's scans.
examples.cn: 团队讨论了病人的扫描结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地是咖死”——地上咖啡洒了，大家围过来议论 → discuss 讨论

root: 拉丁语 discutere“打碎、摇散”，由 dis-“分开”+ quatere“摇”构成；晚期拉丁语转为“审查、讨论”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of discuss, all built on one act: turning a subject over so its parts separate. The setting can be a meeting, a parliament, a book, a clinic, a negotiation, or a classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: discuss 的八个义项都建立在一个动作上：翻动一个话题，使各部分分开。场景可以是会议、议会、书本、诊所、谈判或课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group at a table breaking a problem into pieces and examining each one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人围桌把问题拆成块，逐一检视。

branches.en: TALK: the everyday form, in meetings, over lunch, or in class.
branches.cn: 交谈：日常形式，在会议、午餐或课堂上。

branches.en: DEBATE AND DECIDE: argument shakes options apart until one can be chosen.
branches.cn: 辩论与决定：论证把选项摇散，直到能选出其一。

branches.en: WRITTEN TREATMENT: a chapter examines a subject for readers with no live exchange.
branches.cn: 书面论述：一章为读者检视主题，没有现场交流。

branches.en: CLINICAL: specialists review evidence together and form a shared judgment.
branches.cn: 临床：专家共同复核证据，形成共同判断。

branches.en: NEGOTIATION: terms are examined clause by clause until both sides agree.
branches.cn: 谈判：逐条检视条件，直到双方同意。

intro.en: Discuss is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -able, -ant, -er, -ed, -ing, and the negative prefix un- to build its family.
intro.cn: discuss 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-able、-ant、-er、-ed、-ing，以及否定前缀 un- 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin discutere 'shake apart' shares quatere with quash, concussion, and percussion. The participle stem discuss- gives discussion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discutere“摇散”与 quash、concussion、percussion 共享 quatere。分词词干 discuss- 生成 discussion。

items.meaning: the act of exchanging views; a written treatment of a subject
items.meaningCN: 讨论；论述（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: able or suitable to be discussed
a person who comments on a paper or topic, especially at a conference
items.meaningCN: 讨论者；评论人（-ant 表示人）

items.meaning: a person who discusses
having been talked about or examined
the act of discussing
not talked about or examined

definition_zh: 展示；陈列；显示；表露；显示屏
definition_en: to put something where it can be seen, or to show a quality, feeling, or image
core_image: 一面折叠的旗子被完全展开
scene: 博物馆的玻璃展柜里放着青铜器，射灯照着说明牌。 In the museum the curator displayed the bronze vessel in a glass case.
sceneCN: 这里 display 是「陈列、展示」（第 1 个义项：把某物放在可见处）；句意：博物馆里，策展人把青铜器陈列在玻璃展柜中。

senses.title: Put something where it can be seen
senses.definition: to arrange an object so that people can look at it
senses.definitionCN: 摆放物品让人们观看
senses.example: The museum displays ancient coins.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆陈列古代钱币。
senses.why: The word's first image is a banner unfurled. Old French desploiir meant 'unfold, spread out', so display is what happens when a folded thing is opened to view.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初的意象是展开的旗帜。古法语 desploiir 意为“展开、铺开”，所以 display 就是折叠之物被打开给人看。

senses.title: Show a quality or feeling
senses.definition: to let a quality, emotion, or attitude be seen
senses.definitionCN: 让某种品质、情绪或态度被看见
senses.example: He displayed no fear.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有表现出恐惧。
senses.why: An inner state is treated as a flag: it is displayed when it becomes visible to others. The word shifts from objects to signals of character.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态被当作一面旗：当它对别人可见时，就被 display 出来。这个词从物件转向性格信号。

senses.title: Show information on a screen
senses.definition: to present data or images on an electronic screen
senses.definitionCN: 在电子屏幕上呈现数据或图像
senses.example: The screen displays the time.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕显示时间。
senses.why: The modern screen sense keeps the original 'spread before the eyes'. A display is a surface that unfolds information for a viewer.
senses.whyCN: 现代屏幕义保留最初的“铺开在眼前”。display 就是把信息展开给观看者的表面。

senses.title: An exhibition or show
senses.definition: an arrangement of objects or effects for people to see
senses.definitionCN: 为观看者布置的物品或效果
senses.example: We saw a fireworks display.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看了一场烟花表演。
senses.why: The noun names the whole arranged spectacle, not one object. What is displayed is the collection, and the event is the display.
senses.whyCN: 名词指整个被布置的景观，而非单件物品。被展示的是集合，事件本身则是 display。

senses.title: Show off
senses.definition: to show something in order to impress others
senses.definitionCN: 展示某物以给别人留下印象
senses.example: He likes to display his knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢炫耀自己的知识。
senses.why: The same act can be aimed at admiration rather than information. When the purpose is the audience's reaction, display becomes showing off.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作可以是为了赞赏而非告知。当目的是观众的反应，display 就变成炫耀。

senses.title: A courtship display in biology
senses.definition: a set of movements or colors an animal uses to attract a mate
senses.definitionCN: 动物用来吸引配偶的动作或色彩
senses.example: The bird's display attracts mates.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟的展示吸引配偶。
senses.why: Biology borrows the exhibition image: feathers, calls, and movements are arranged to be seen by a specific audience. The display is an evolved advertisement.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用展览意象：羽毛、鸣叫与动作被安排给特定观众看。这种展示是演化出来的广告。

senses.title: A show of force or strength
senses.definition: a deliberate public demonstration of power or capability
senses.definitionCN: 有意公开显示力量或能力
senses.example: The fleet held a display of strength.
senses.exampleCN: 舰队进行了一次力量展示。
senses.why: A military display is addressed to rivals: the thing shown is capability, and the audience is meant to be warned rather than entertained.
senses.whyCN: 军事展示的对象是对手：展示的是能力，观众是被警告而非被取悦的。

senses.title: A computer monitor
senses.definition: an electronic device that shows images and text
senses.definitionCN: 显示图像与文字的电子设备
senses.example: She bought a high-resolution display.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一台高分辨率显示器。
senses.why: The device is named by its function: it is the surface on which information is unfolded. The noun has become a physical object.
senses.whyCN: 这种设备以其功能命名：它是信息被展开的表面。名词已经变成一个实体物件。

senses.title: Unfurl a flag or banner
senses.definition: in the original sense, to unfold a flag, sail, or banner
senses.definitionCN: 最初义：展开旗帜、帆或横幅
senses.example: The crew displayed the flag.
senses.exampleCN: 船员展开了旗帜。
senses.why: c. 1300 the verb meant 'unfold, spread out, unfurl' a banner. Properly of sails or flags, the word was unconnected to play, despite the similar sound.
senses.whyCN: 约 1300 年，动词意为“展开、铺开、扬起”旗帜。它本用于帆或旗，尽管读音像 play，却与 play 无关。

intro.en: Display began with cloth: a folded flag or sail spread open. The literal unfolding became the model for showing objects, feelings, screens, and power.
intro.cn: display 从布开始：折叠的旗或帆被展开。字面的展开成为展示物品、情绪、屏幕与力量的模型。

items.en: display means 'unfold, spread out, unfurl' a banner or sail.
items.cn: display 意为“展开、铺开、扬起”旗帜或帆。

items.en: From desploiir (Modern French déployer) 'unfold, unfasten, spread out'.
items.cn: 来自 desploiir（现代法语 déployer）“展开、解开、铺开”。

items.en: From Latin displicare 'to scatter', in Medieval Latin 'to unfold', from dis- 'un-, apart' + plicare 'to fold'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 displicare“散开”，中世纪拉丁语中作“展开”，由 dis-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”构成。

items.en: plicare belongs to PIE *plek- 'to plait', also behind ply, fold, and complex.
items.cn: plicare 属于原始印欧语 *plek-“编织”，也是 ply、fold、complex 的来源。

items.en: The meaning 'reveal, exhibit, expose to view' appears; the sense 'allow to be seen unintentionally' also develops.
items.cn: “揭示、展出、暴露于视野”的义项出现；同时发展出“无意中让人看见”的义项。

note.en: The first group is about words that look or sound close; the second is about verbs that also put something before an audience.
note.cn: 第一组看形近或音近的词，第二组看同样把某物呈现给观众的动词。

entries.definition: to spread out troops or resources for use. It comes from the same Latin plicare family, through French.
entries.definitionCN: 展开部队或资源以供使用。它出自同一个拉丁 plicare 词族，经法语传入。

entries.definition: to annoy or dissatisfy someone. It sounds close but comes from dis- + please.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不快。读音相近，但来自 dis- + please。

entries.definition: the past tense and past participle of display.
entries.definitionCN: display 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: to make something visible or known. It is the broadest and most neutral verb in this group.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物可见或为人知。它是这组里最宽泛、最中性的动词。

entries.definition: to show something in a public place or in a formal way. It is close to display but more institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 在公共场所或正式地展示。它接近 display，但更机构化。

entries.definition: to show something by giving evidence or an example. It adds the idea of proving.
entries.definitionCN: 通过证据或例子展示。它增加了“证明”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Real links: the flag-unfolding image, the shared root with deploy, the screen sense, and the biology sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：展开旗帜的意象、与 deploy 的共同词根、屏幕义，以及生物学义。

normal.en: c. 1300 display meant to unfurl a flag. Anything shown is mentally unfolded like cloth.
normal.cn: 约 1300 年 display 意为展开旗帜。任何被展示之物都在心里像布一样被铺开。

normal.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' is the base; dis- reverses it. Display is the opposite of folding.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plicare“折叠”是词基；dis- 反转它。display 就是折叠的反面。

normal.en: Deploy and display share the same root: both spread something out for use or view.
normal.cn: deploy 与 display 共享同一词根：两者都把某物铺开以供使用或观看。

normal.en: A screen display unfolds information on a surface, the same image applied to pixels.
normal.cn: 屏幕 display 在表面上展开信息，同一意象用在像素上。

normal.en: A bird's courtship display is an evolved advertisement, arranged to be seen by one audience.
normal.cn: 鸟的求偶展示是演化出的广告，为特定观众安排可见。

abstract.en: Display is control of visibility: the object is placed, lit, and framed so that others must see it.
abstract.cn: 展示是可见性的控制：物件被摆放、打光、装框，使别人不得不看见。

abstract.en: Showing a quality and showing off differ only in intended audience response, not in the act of showing.
abstract.cn: 表露品质与炫耀只差在意图中的观众反应，不在展示动作本身。

abstract.en: Every display creates a gap between what is shown and what is withheld; the frame is part of the meaning.
abstract.cn: 每次展示都在“所示”与“所隐”之间造出落差；框本身就是意义的一部分。

examples.en: The museum displays ancient coins.
examples.cn: 博物馆陈列古代钱币。

examples.en: He displayed no fear.
examples.cn: 他没有表现出恐惧。

examples.en: The screen displays the time.
examples.cn: 屏幕显示时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地是铺雷”——把东西铺开，像雷一样引人看 → display 展示

root: 古法语 desploiir“展开”，来自拉丁语 displicare“散开、展开”，由 dis- + plicare“折叠”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of display, all built on one act: unfolding something so it can be seen. What unfolds can be a flag, an object, a feeling, information on a screen, or a show of power.
sensesIntro.cn: display 的九个义项都建立在一个动作上：把某物展开，使其可见。展开的可以是旗帜、物件、情绪、屏幕信息，或力量的展示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded flag unfurled until the whole surface is visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面折叠的旗被展开，整个表面可见。

branches.en: EXHIBIT: objects and flags are unfolded for people to look at.
branches.cn: 展出：物件与旗帜被展开供人观看。

branches.en: SHOW QUALITY: an inner state or knowledge is unfolded for an audience, sincerely or for effect.
branches.cn: 表露品质：内在状态或知识向观众展开，真诚或为效果。

branches.en: SCREEN: information is unfolded on a surface, and the surface itself becomes a device.
branches.cn: 屏幕：信息在表面上展开，表面本身成为设备。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: an animal's body and behavior are arranged as an advertisement.
branches.cn: 生物学：动物的身体与行为被安排成广告。

branches.en: FORCE: capability is displayed to warn rivals rather than to entertain.
branches.cn: 武力：能力被展示以警告对手，而非取悦。

intro.en: Display is both verb and noun. English adds -able, -ed, -ing, -er, and the prefixes re- and self-, plus the negative un-.
intro.cn: display 既是动词也是名词。英语加 -able、-ed、-ing、-er，以及前缀 re-、self- 和否定 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin displicare 'unfold' shares plicare 'to fold' with deploy, ply, apply, and complex. The English word arrived through Old French, not directly from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 displicare“展开”与 deploy、ply、apply、complex 共享 plicare“折叠”。英语词经古法语传入，而非直接来自拉丁语。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 展开部队或资源（同源英语词）

definition_zh: 排列；布置；使倾向于；处置；处理掉；变卖；吃掉；消灭
definition_en: to arrange things in their proper places, to make someone inclined toward something, or to deal with and get rid of something
core_image: 一张长桌上，餐具被逐一摆到该在的位置，用完后又一件件撤走
scene: 回收点旁堆着一箱旧电池。 The staff disposed of the old batteries at the collection point.
sceneCN: 这里 dispose 是「处理掉、丢弃」（第 4 个义项：把某物清走）；句意：工作人员在回收点处理掉了那些旧电池。

senses.title: Arrange in proper positions
senses.definition: to place people or things in the positions they should occupy
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物放到各自应在的位置
senses.example: The general disposed his troops along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 将军沿河部署部队。
senses.why: Latin disponere is dis- 'apart' plus ponere 'to place': the verb literally means 'place apart', giving each item its own slot. English took this as the primary sense in the late 14c.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 disponere 是 dis-“分开”+ ponere“放置”：字面就是“分开放置”，给每件东西一个槽位。14 世纪末英语以此为主要义。

senses.title: Set affairs in order
senses.definition: to arrange or settle plans, affairs, or a piece of business
senses.definitionCN: 安排或料理计划、事务或一桩事情
senses.example: He disposed his affairs before the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 他在出行前把事务安排妥当。
senses.why: The object turns abstract: plans are placed into their right order rather than physically moved. This sense now survives mainly in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 对象变得抽象：计划被“摆”进正确的次序，而不是被物理移动。这个义项现在主要见于正式书面语。

senses.title: Incline someone toward something
senses.definition: to make someone likely or willing to feel or do something
senses.definitionCN: 使人可能或愿意产生某种感受、做某事
senses.example: The evidence disposed the jury to doubt him.
senses.exampleCN: 证据使陪审团倾向于怀疑他。
senses.why: A mind is treated as a surface on which a bias is placed. From the 17c. the verb means to put someone in a certain frame of mind, and the participle disposed keeps this alive.
senses.whyCN: 心智被当作一块可以放上偏向的表面。17 世纪起这个词表示把人放进某种心境，分词 disposed 让这一义延续至今。

senses.title: Get rid of something
senses.definition: in dispose of, to throw away, destroy, or remove something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 用于 dispose of，表示丢弃、销毁或清除不需要的东西
senses.example: The factory must dispose of its chemical waste safely.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂必须安全处理化学废料。
senses.why: To dispose of is to place something away: the old sense of placing becomes placing out of your hands, so the object leaves your responsibility. Recorded from the mid-15c.
senses.whyCN: dispose of 就是把东西“放到别处”：古老的“放置”变成“放到你手之外”，物件于是离开你的责任范围。15 世纪中期已有记录。

senses.title: Deal with and settle a matter
senses.definition: in dispose of, to finish or settle a question, case, or task
senses.definitionCN: 用于 dispose of，表示结束或了结一个问题、案件或任务
senses.example: The committee disposed of the complaint in ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会十分钟就了结了这起投诉。
senses.why: Once a matter is placed, it is out of the way; finishing becomes a kind of clearing. The same phrase covers physical removal and administrative closure.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被“放好”就不再挡路；完成因此成了一种清理。同一个短语既指物理移除，也指行政了结。

senses.title: Sell or transfer property
senses.definition: in dispose of, to sell, give away, or otherwise transfer ownership
senses.definitionCN: 用于 dispose of，表示出售、赠予或以其他方式转让所有权
senses.example: The estate disposed of several paintings at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 该遗产管理方在拍卖会上变卖了数幅画作。
senses.why: Selling is a legal form of getting rid: the object leaves your ownership. Commercial English fixed dispose of as the standard phrase for transfer of property.
senses.whyCN: 出售是“摆脱”的法律形式：物件离开你的所有权。商业英语把 dispose of 固定为转让财产的标准说法。

senses.title: Consume food or supplies
senses.definition: in dispose of, informal: to eat or consume something completely
senses.definitionCN: 用于 dispose of，非正式：把食物或用品吃光用光
senses.example: The team disposed of three pizzas in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 团队一小时内吃光了三张披萨。
senses.why: Eating destroys the object and clears it from the table, so the get-rid-of sense extends to consumption. The tone is informal and slightly humorous.
senses.whyCN: 吃会毁掉对象、把它从桌上清走，于是“处理掉”的义项延伸到消耗。语气非正式，略带玩笑。

senses.title: Kill or eliminate someone
senses.definition: euphemistic: to kill or get rid of a person
senses.definitionCN: 委婉语：杀死或除掉某人
senses.example: The villain disposed of the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 那个反派除掉了证人。
senses.why: The darkest extension of get rid of: a person is treated as an obstacle to be removed. The euphemism works because the verb keeps its neutral, administrative tone.
senses.whyCN: 这是“处理掉”最黑暗的延伸：人被当作需要移除的障碍。委婉之所以成立，是因为动词保持着中性的行政口吻。

senses.title: Have something available for use
senses.definition: in dispose of, formal: to have something at your command or available
senses.definitionCN: 用于 dispose of，正式：拥有某物可供调遣或使用
senses.example: The library disposes of a large map collection.
senses.exampleCN: 该图书馆拥有大量地图藏品可供使用。
senses.why: A shift from removal to availability: what you may place freely is what you control. The phrase at one's disposal turns the same idea into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 从移除转向可用：你能自由“摆放”的东西，就是你掌控的东西。短语 at one's disposal 把同一想法变成名词。

senses.title: Bestow or assign something
senses.definition: archaic: to give or assign something to a person
senses.definitionCN: 古义：把某物给予或分配给某人
senses.example: In old wills, land was disposed to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧遗嘱中，土地被授予长子。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant 'to bestow'. English kept this giving sense alongside removal; modern usage has largely replaced it with bequeath or assign.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词也有“授予”义。英语在“移除”之外保留了这一给予义；现代用法大多已改用 bequeath 或 assign。

intro.en: Dispose entered English through Old French as a word about order. Its Latin parts are dis- 'apart' and ponere 'to place', and every later sense grows from the act of putting things where they belong.
intro.cn: dispose 经古法语进入英语，本是一句关于“次序”的话。它的拉丁构件是 dis-“分开”与 ponere“放置”，后来所有义项都从“把东西放到该在的位置”生长出来。

items.en: First recorded as 'arrange, set in order, distribute', borrowed from Old French disposer.
items.cn: 最早记录为“排列、整顿、分配”，借自古法语 disposer。

items.en: disposer 'to arrange, order' is a direct reflex of Latin disponere, with the same prefix and verb.
items.cn: 古法语 disposer“安排、整顿”是拉丁语 disponere 的直接反映，前缀与动词相同。

items.en: disponere 'to arrange, manage' = dis- 'apart' + ponere 'to put, place'. Ponere also gives position, deposit, compose, and postpone.
items.cn: disponere“安排、管理”= dis-“分开”+ ponere“放置”。ponere 还生成 position、deposit、compose、postpone。

items.en: The phrasal verb dispose of appears with the sense 'get rid of, put away'.
items.cn: 短语动词 dispose of 出现，义为“处理掉、收起来”。

items.en: 'To incline or make willing' is recorded; the participle disposed becomes a common adjective for mood and tendency.
items.cn: “使倾向于、使愿意”被记录；分词 disposed 成为表示心境与倾向的常用形容词。

items.en: Modern English splits the word: bare dispose is formal 'arrange' or 'incline', while almost every everyday sense lives in dispose of.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分开：单独的 dispose 是正式的“安排”或“使倾向”，几乎所有日常义都住在 dispose of 里。

note.en: The first group shares spelling and morphology with dispose; the second is about verbs that also mean putting things in order or getting rid of them.
note.cn: 第一组与 dispose 共享拼写与构词，第二组看同样表示“整理”或“丢弃”的动词。

entries.definition: the act of getting rid of something. It is dispose plus -al.
entries.definitionCN: 处理；处置。它是 dispose 加 -al。

entries.definition: inclined or arranged. It is the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于的；已布置的。它是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: a person's usual mood, or an arrangement. It comes from Latin dispositio.
entries.definitionCN: 性情；安排。来自拉丁语 dispositio。

entries.definition: to throw something away as useless. It is sharper and more final than dispose of.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物当废物扔掉。它比 dispose of 更干脆、更终结。

entries.definition: to put things in a neat or planned order. It covers the first sense but has no get-rid-of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西排成整齐或计划好的次序。它覆盖第一义，却没有“处理掉”之义。

entries.definition: to give resources to a purpose. It matches the bestow sense, not removal.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分配给某用途。它对应“授予”义，而非移除。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin ponere 'to place', the phrasal verb dispose of, the adjective disposed, and the idiom at one's disposal.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 ponere“放置”、短语动词 dispose of、形容词 disposed，以及习语 at one's disposal。

normal.en: Latin ponere means 'to place'. Dispose is to place things apart, each into its own slot.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为“放置”。dispose 就是把东西分开放，各归其位。

normal.en: Dispose of is 'place away': the object leaves your hands, and that is why the phrase means get rid of.
normal.cn: dispose of 是“放到远处”：东西离开你的手，所以这个短语表示处理掉。

normal.en: At your disposal means inside your placing: what you may move freely is what you control.
normal.cn: at your disposal 意为“在你可摆放的范围内”：你能自由搬动的东西，就是你能支配的东西。

normal.en: Disposed describes where your mind was placed: evidence disposes you toward doubt or trust.
normal.cn: disposed 描述你的心被放到了哪一边：证据使你倾向于怀疑或信任。

normal.en: A general disposes troops, a butler disposes plates, a company disposes of waste — one verb, three scales.
normal.cn: 将军部署部队、管家摆放餐盘、公司处理废料——同一个动词，三种尺度。

abstract.en: Order and removal are one gesture: putting something in its right place also means taking it out of the wrong one.
abstract.cn: 次序与移除是同一个手势：把东西放到对的位置，也就把它从错的位置拿走。

abstract.en: Control is measured by what you may dispose of; ownership is the right to move things away.
abstract.cn: 掌控由你能处置的东西来衡量；所有权就是把东西移走的权利。

abstract.en: The word hides violence inside administration: to dispose of a witness sounds like paperwork.
abstract.cn: 这个词把暴力藏在行政语言里：dispose of a witness 听起来像在办手续。

examples.en: The general disposed his troops in a crescent formation.
examples.cn: 将军把部队布置成月牙阵。

examples.en: Please dispose of used batteries properly.
examples.cn: 请妥善处理废旧电池。

examples.en: She is well disposed toward the proposal.
examples.cn: 她对这项提议抱有好感。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地石铺”——把石头一块块铺到该在的位置 → dispose 排列、布置、处置

root: 拉丁语 disponere“分开放置”，由 dis-“分开”+ ponere“放置”构成；同族有 position、deposit、compose、postpone。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of dispose, all turning on Latin ponere 'to place'. The word places things in order, places a bias in a mind, and finally places things away — which is why dispose of means get rid of.
sensesIntro.cn: dispose 的十个义项都绕着拉丁语 ponere“放置”转。它把东西摆成次序，把偏向放进心里，最后把东西放到远处——所以 dispose of 表示处理掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: placing each thing where it belongs, then placing it away.
core.cn: 核心意象：把每件东西放到该在的位置，再把它放到远处。

branches.en: ORDER: people, troops, and affairs are given their proper positions.
branches.cn: 次序：人、部队与事务被放到各自应有的位置。

branches.en: INCLINE: a bias is placed in the mind, so a person becomes disposed toward something.
branches.cn: 倾向：一种偏向被放进心里，于是人被“摆”向某事。

branches.en: REMOVE: what is placed away leaves your hands, from rubbish to a whole meal.
branches.cn: 移除：被“放走”的东西离开你的手，从垃圾到一整餐。

branches.en: CONTROL: settling a case or holding resources is having them inside your placing.
branches.cn: 掌控：了结一案或握有资源，就是让它们在你可摆放的范围内。

branches.en: TRANSFER: property passes to a buyer, a person is eliminated, or goods are bestowed.
branches.cn: 转移：财产转给买家，人被清除，或物品被授予。

intro.en: Dispose is a Latin verb that English expanded with -al, -able, -er, and the prefixes in-, pre-, and re-. The core ponere also builds position and deposit.
intro.cn: dispose 是拉丁动词，英语用 -al、-able、-er 以及前缀 in-、pre-、re- 扩展它。核心的 ponere 还构成 position 与 deposit。

latinIntro.en: Latin disponere 'arrange' and ponere 'place' sit beside compositus, depositus, and positio. The prefix dis- marks separation, which is why the word begins with arrangement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 disponere“安排”与 ponere“放置”旁边是 compositus、depositus、positio。前缀 dis- 标记分离，所以这个词从“排列”开始。

items.meaning: the act of getting rid of something; the power to use it
items.meaningCN: 处理；处置；使用权（-al 构成名词）

items.meaning: made to be thrown away after use; available to spend
a person's usual character; an arrangement
items.meaningCN: 性情；安排（源自拉丁 dispositio）

items.meaning: inclined or arranged in a certain way
a device or person that gets rid of waste
slightly unwell; unwilling
items.meaningCN: 身体不适的；不情愿的（in- 否定）

items.meaning: to make someone inclined in advance
items.meaningCN: 使预先倾向于（pre- 表“先”）
items.example: genes predispose some people to the disease
items.exampleCN: 基因使某些人易患此病

items.meaning: to arrange again
deciding a matter; final

definition_zh: 截然不同的；分开的；清晰可辨的；明显的；确切的；独特的
definition_en: clearly different or separate, and therefore easy to perceive or recognize
core_image: 画布上两种颜色被一条干净的线分开，互不渗染
scene: 显微镜下，两种细胞的边缘被染色剂标出。 Under the microscope the edges of the two cells were distinct, and a thin line separated their outlines.
sceneCN: 这里 distinct 是「清晰可辨的」（第 3 个义项：轮廓分明、易于感知）；句意：显微镜下，两种细胞的边缘清晰可辨，一条细线把它们的轮廓分开。

pos.zh: 不同的；分开的；清晰的；明显的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Different in kind, not the same
senses.titleCN: 截然不同的；种类上不同
senses.definition: clearly different in kind or identity from something else
senses.definitionCN: 在种类或身份上与他物明显不同
senses.example: Hares and rabbits are distinct species.
senses.exampleCN: 野兔和家兔是不同的物种。
senses.why: The Latin participle distinctus means 'separated'. Two things that are distinct have been marked off from each other, so their difference is not a matter of degree but of boundary.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词 distinctus 意为“被分开的”。两物 distinct，就是被彼此划开了，所以它们的差别不是程度问题，而是边界问题。

senses.title: Separate as an individual entity
senses.definition: existing as a separate thing, not part of the other
senses.definitionCN: 作为独立之物存在，不属于另一物
senses.example: The two problems are distinct and need separate answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个问题是独立的，需要分别作答。
senses.why: Here the word stresses separateness rather than dissimilarity: each item stands on its own. This is the sense behind distinct accounts, distinct layers, and distinct legal offences.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调的是“分开”而非“不同”：每一项都独立成立。独立的账户、独立的层、独立的罪名都用这个义。

senses.title: Clearly perceived by the senses
senses.definition: easy to see, hear, smell, or feel; not blurred
senses.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见、嗅到或感觉到；不模糊
senses.example: A distinct smell of coffee came from the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房里传来一股清晰的咖啡香。
senses.why: From the 14c. the word describes what stands out sharply to perception. A distinct outline is one whose edges are marked, so the boundary sense becomes a sensory one.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪起，这个词描述在感知中鲜明突出的东西。distinct 的轮廓就是边缘被标记出来的轮廓，于是“边界”义变成“感官清晰”义。

senses.title: Unmistakable and definite
senses.definition: strong enough to be recognized without doubt
senses.definitionCN: 强到可以被认出而无疑
senses.example: There is a distinct possibility of rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚确有可能下雨。
senses.why: A quantity or chance that is distinct is not vague: it can be pointed to. The word moves from clear edges to clear evidence, giving the sense 'definite, decided'.
senses.whyCN: distinct 的数量或可能性不含糊：它指得出来。这个词从清晰的边缘走向清晰的证据，产生“确切、明确”的义。

senses.title: Noticeable and significant
senses.definition: clearly noticeable, often in a way that matters
senses.definitionCN: 明显可察，且往往重要
senses.example: The new policy made a distinct improvement in morale.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策明显改善了士气。
senses.why: When an improvement is distinct, it is large enough to be separated from background noise. The perceptual sense shades into evaluation: clear enough to count.
senses.whyCN: 改善如果 distinct，就大到能从背景噪声中分离出来。感知义滑向评价义：清楚到值得计数。

senses.title: Clearly outlined in shape
senses.definition: having a sharp, well-marked edge or outline
senses.definitionCN: 边缘或轮廓清晰锐利
senses.example: The mountain stood distinct against the evening sky.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山在暮色中轮廓分明。
senses.why: This is the most physical use: the eye separates figure from ground because the edge is sharp. It is the source image from which the abstract senses borrow clarity.
senses.whyCN: 这是最物理的用法：因为边缘锐利，眼睛把图形与背景分开。它是源意象，抽象义都从这里借来“清晰”。

senses.title: Individual and characteristic
senses.definition: having a quality that belongs to one thing and marks it out
senses.definitionCN: 具有只属于某物、能把它标出的性质
senses.example: Each region has a distinct accent.
senses.exampleCN: 每个地区都有独特的口音。
senses.why: A distinct accent is both separate from other accents and recognizable as this one. The word joins difference with identity, which is why it often appears with 'characteristic'.
senses.whyCN: distinct 的口音既与其他口音分开，又能被认作这一种。这个词把差异与身份合在一起，所以常与 characteristic 连用。

senses.title: Clearly articulated in speech
senses.definition: of sounds or words, produced clearly enough to be separated by the ear
senses.definitionCN: 声音或词被发得足够清楚，能被耳朵分辨
senses.example: She spoke in distinct syllables.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话音节清晰。
senses.why: Phonetics uses the word for sounds that do not run together. Distinct articulation is literally a series of marked boundaries in sound.
senses.whyCN: 语音学用它指不粘连的声音。distinct 的发音就是声音里一连串被标记出的边界。

senses.title: Set in contrast: as distinct from
senses.definition: in the phrase as distinct from, used to keep two ideas apart
senses.definitionCN: 用于 as distinct from，把两个概念分开
senses.example: The role is advisory, as distinct from executive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个角色是顾问性的，与执行性角色不同。
senses.why: The phrase turns the adjective into a logical tool: it asks the listener to hold two categories apart. The boundary sense becomes an argumentative move.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把形容词变成逻辑工具：它要求听者把两个类别分开握住。“边界”义变成一种论辩动作。

intro.en: Distinct is the past participle of Latin distinguere, borrowed whole into English. Its history is a history of boundaries: first a physical mark, then a clear edge, then a clear idea.
intro.cn: distinct 是拉丁语 distinguere 的过去分词，整体借入英语。它的历史就是边界的历史：先是物理标记，再是清晰边缘，最后是清晰观念。

items.en: Borrowed from Latin distinctus, past participle of distinguere, with the sense 'different, separate'.
items.cn: 从拉丁语 distinctus 借入，即 distinguere 的过去分词，义为“不同的、分开的”。

items.en: distinguere 'to separate, mark off, distinguish' = dis- 'apart' + -stinguere. Related English words include distinguish, instinct, and extinguish.
items.cn: distinguere“分开、标记、区别”= dis-“分开”+ -stinguere。相关英语词有 distinguish、instinct、extinguish。

items.en: The meaning of -stinguere is disputed. Some trace it to a root meaning 'to prick, mark', others to 'to push'. The dictionaries agree on the family but not on the underlying image.
items.cn: -stinguere 的含义有争议。有人追溯到“刺、标记”的词根，也有人释为“推”。各家同意词族归属，却不同意底层意象。

items.en: The senses 'not identical' and 'clearly perceived' are both established in Middle English.
items.cn: “不相同”与“清晰感知”两个义项在中古英语中均已确立。

items.en: The sense 'unmistakable, decided' is recorded, especially with quantities and possibilities.
items.cn: “确切的、明确的”义被记录，尤其用于数量与可能性。

items.en: Modern English keeps both halves: distinct species (separate) and a distinct smell (clear). The adverb distinctly carries the perceptual side.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两半：distinct species（分开）与 a distinct smell（清晰）。副词 distinctly 承载感知的一面。

note.en: The first group is about words built from the same Latin stem; the second is about adjectives that also mark difference or clarity.
note.cn: 第一组看同一拉丁词干构成的词，第二组看同样标记“差异”或“清晰”的形容词。

entries.definition: marking a thing as different and recognizable. It adds -ive to the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物显得不同且可辨识的。它是同一词干加 -ive。

entries.definition: a difference, or a mark of excellence. It is the noun of action from distinguere.
entries.definitionCN: 差别；卓越。它是 distinguere 的动作名词。

entries.definition: to tell two things apart. It is the English verb from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 区分两物。它是同一拉丁动词的英语动词形式。

entries.definition: not joined or connected. It stresses physical or social division, not clarity.
entries.definitionCN: 不连在一起的。它强调物理或社会分隔，而非清晰。

entries.definition: easy to see or understand. It shares the clarity sense but not the difference sense.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见或理解。它共享“清晰”义，没有“差异”义。

entries.definition: fixed and certain. It matches the unmistakable sense but lacks the boundary image.
entries.definitionCN: 确定而无疑。它对应“明确”义，但缺少边界意象。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin distinguere 'mark off', the two halves of the word (separate and clear), and the phrase as distinct from.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 distinguere“标记分开”、这个词的两半（分开与清晰），以及短语 as distinct from。

normal.en: Latin distinguere means 'mark off'. Distinct things have been marked apart from each other.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 distinguere 意为“标记分开”。distinct 的东西就是被彼此标开的。

normal.en: The word has two halves: separate (distinct species) and clear (a distinct smell). Both come from the same boundary image.
normal.cn: 这个词有两半：分开（distinct species）与清晰（a distinct smell）。两者都来自同一个边界意象。

normal.en: A distinct outline is one whose edge you can point to; a distinct idea is one whose edge you can state.
normal.cn: distinct 的轮廓，是你能指出边缘的轮廓；distinct 的观念，是你能说出边界的观念。

normal.en: As distinct from is a boundary in an argument: it keeps two categories from melting together.
normal.cn: as distinct from 是论证里的一条边界：它防止两个类别融化在一起。

normal.en: Distinctly is the adverb of the senses: you hear, see, or remember something distinctly.
normal.cn: distinctly 是感官的副词：你清楚地听见、看见或记得某事。

abstract.en: Identity needs a boundary: something becomes a distinct thing only by being cut away from everything else.
abstract.cn: 身份需要边界：一物只有被从其余一切中切开，才成为 distinct 的东西。

abstract.en: Clarity is social as well as optical: a distinct voice is one the group can separate from the noise.
abstract.cn: 清晰既是光学的也是社会的：distinct 的声音，是群体能从噪声中分开的声音。

abstract.en: The same word serves difference and excellence: to be distinct is to be separate, and often to be better.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼任差异与卓越：distinct 既是分开，也常常是更好。

examples.en: The two theories are quite distinct.
examples.cn: 这两种理论截然不同。

examples.en: There is a distinct smell of smoke in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里有明显的烟味。

examples.en: Her writing has a distinct style of its own.
examples.cn: 她的写作有自己独特的风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: “敌视听客特”——把敌人和听客特意分开 → distinct 截然不同的、清晰的

root: 拉丁语 distinguere“分开、标记、区别”的过去分词 distinctus，由 dis-“分开”+ -stinguere（含义存疑）构成；同族有 distinguish、instinct、extinguish。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of distinct, all built on a boundary. The boundary can be between species, between things, between a figure and its background, or between two ideas in an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: distinct 的九个义项都建立在一条边界上。这条边界可以在物种之间、事物之间、图形与背景之间，或论证中的两个观念之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean line that marks one thing off from another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把一物与他物划开的清晰界线。

branches.en: SEPARATE: difference in kind, and independent existence as its own thing.
branches.cn: 分开：种类上的差异，以及作为独立之物的存在。

branches.en: PERCEIVE: a marked edge makes a thing easy to see, hear, or articulate.
branches.cn: 感知：被标记的边缘使某物易于看见、听见或清晰发音。

branches.en: CERTAIN: clear enough to be pointed to becomes definite enough to count.
branches.cn: 确定：清楚到可以指认，就变成确凿到值得计数。

branches.en: IDENTITY: a distinct quality belongs to one thing and marks it out.
branches.cn: 身份：distinct 的性质属于某物，并把它标出。

branches.en: CONTRAST: as distinct from uses the boundary as a tool of argument.
branches.cn: 对比：as distinct from 把边界当作论证工具。

intro.en: Distinct is an adjective from a Latin participle. English adds -ly, -ness, -ion, and -ive, and builds the verb distinguish from the same Latin stem.
intro.cn: distinct 是来自拉丁分词的形容词。英语加 -ly、-ness、-ion、-ive，并用同一拉丁词干构成动词 distinguish。

latinIntro.en: Latin distinguere 'mark off' produced distinctus 'separated' and distinctio 'a division'. The same verb family includes instinct and extinguish, whose histories diverge sharply from distinct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 distinguere“标记分开”生成 distinctus“已分开”与 distinctio“划分”。同一动词家族还有 instinct 与 extinguish，它们的历史与 distinct 分道扬镳。

the quality of being clear or separate

items.meaning: marking something as different and recognizable
able to be told apart
