definition_zh: 分发；分配；散布；销售配送；使分布；分类排列；（数学）分配律
definition_en: to give out or spread something among people, places, or groups, often in portions
core_image: 一只手把一把种子均匀撒进几块田里，每块都落得一些
scene: 会场入口，志愿者抱着一叠传单，旁边的空箱子还敞着口。 At the entrance the volunteers distributed leaflets to everyone who came into the hall, and the pile soon thinned.
sceneCN: 这里 distribute 是「分发」（第 1 个义项：把东西逐份给人）；句意：入口处，志愿者把传单分发给每一个进入会场的人，那叠纸很快变薄。

senses.title: Give out to each person
senses.definition: to give a share of something to each person in a group
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的一份给群体中的每个人
senses.example: Volunteers distributed blankets to the refugees.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者向难民分发毯子。
senses.why: Latin distribuere means 'deal out in portions'. The prefix dis- here means 'in different directions', so the act is one of splitting a whole among many receivers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 distribuere 意为“分份发出去”。前缀 dis- 在这里表示“向不同方向”，所以这个动作是把一个整体分给许多接收者。

senses.title: Spread over an area
senses.definition: to scatter or place something over a space or surface
senses.definitionCN: 把某物撒开或布置在一片空间或表面上
senses.example: The seeds are distributed by the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 种子被风散布开来。
senses.why: When the receivers are places instead of people, the same splitting becomes scattering. A species that is widely distributed has its members spread across a map.
senses.whyCN: 当接收者从人变成地点，同一种“分开”就成了“撒开”。一个广泛分布的物种，其成员散布在地图上。

senses.title: Allot in shares or proportions
senses.definition: to divide something into shares, often according to a rule
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成份额，常按某种规则
senses.example: The profits were distributed among the partners.
senses.exampleCN: 利润在合伙人之间分配。
senses.why: Economics and law need a rule for the split: equal shares, need, or investment. The verb names the operation, while distribution names the resulting pattern.
senses.whyCN: 经济与法律需要一条分配规则：均分、按需或按投入。动词命名操作，名词 distribution 命名结果格局。

senses.title: Supply goods through a network
senses.definition: in business, to move and sell products through wholesalers and retailers
senses.definitionCN: 商业中，通过批发商与零售商把产品送到并售出
senses.example: The company distributes its software through local partners.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司通过本地伙伴分销软件。
senses.why: A supply chain is a chain of hands. Distributing is the stage where goods are handed from producer to the points of sale, so the word becomes a commercial function.
senses.whyCN: 供应链是一条手递手的链。distribute 是货物从生产者交到销售点的阶段，于是这个词成了一种商业职能。

senses.title: Reach an audience through media
senses.definition: of a film, book, or broadcast, to be released and made available to the public
senses.definitionCN: 电影、书籍或节目被发行并提供给公众
senses.example: The documentary was distributed to forty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片被发行到四十个国家。
senses.why: Media distribution repeats the same logic: one master copy is split into many prints, files, or signals, each reaching a viewer.
senses.whyCN: 媒体发行重复同一逻辑：一个母版被分成许多拷贝、文件或信号，每一份抵达一个观众。

senses.title: Apply a rule across a set (mathematics)
senses.definition: in mathematics, to multiply a term across each part inside a bracket
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，把一个项乘到括号内的每一项
senses.example: Distribute the 3 over (x + 2) to get 3x + 6.
senses.exampleCN: 把 3 分配到 (x + 2) 上，得到 3x + 6。
senses.why: The distributive law says a × (b + c) = a×b + a×c: the multiplier is 'dealt out' to each addend. The metaphor is exact — one thing is given to every member.
senses.whyCN: 分配律说 a × (b + c) = a×b + a×c：乘数被“发”给每个加数。这个隐喻是精确的——一样东西给了每一个成员。

senses.title: Apply a term to all members (logic)
senses.definition: in logic, of a term, to refer to every member of its class
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中，一个词项指涉其类的每一个成员
senses.example: In 'All men are mortal', the subject term is distributed.
senses.exampleCN: 在“所有人都会死”中，主项是周延的。
senses.why: Medieval logic asked whether a term covers the whole class or only part of it. A distributed term is one whose share reaches every member, the same image as handing out portions.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪逻辑追问一个词项覆盖整个类还是只覆盖一部分。周延的词项，其份额抵达每一个成员，与分发份额是同一意象。

senses.title: Classify and arrange in order
senses.titleCN: 分类排列；分门别类（较旧）
senses.definition: in 16c. usage, to divide things into classes and arrange them
senses.definitionCN: 16 世纪用法：把事物分成类别并加以排列
senses.example: The old herbals distributed plants by leaf shape.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的草药书按叶形把植物分类排列。
senses.why: The 1550s sense was 'classify, arrange in order'. Putting each item into its class is another form of dealing out: every thing receives its category.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 50 年代的义项是“分类、按序排列”。把每件东西放进它的类，是另一种“分发”：每物领到自己的范畴。

senses.title: Occur in a spatial pattern
senses.definition: of data or natural features, to be spread in a measurable pattern
senses.definitionCN: 数据或自然特征以可测量的格局铺开
senses.example: The rainfall is unevenly distributed across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区降雨分布不均。
senses.why: Statistics turns the verb into a description of pattern: not who gives what, but how densely things sit on the ground. Distribution becomes a shape on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这个动词变成对格局的描述：不问谁给谁什么，而问东西在地面上有多密。分布于是成了图表上的形状。

intro.en: Distribute came into English as a word about dealing out shares. Its Latin parts are dis- 'apart' and tribuere 'to allot', a verb tied to the tribe as a unit of division.
intro.cn: distribute 进入英语时是一个关于“分份”的词。它的拉丁构件是 dis-“分开”与 tribuere“分配”，后者与作为分配单位的“部落”有关。

items.en: First recorded as 'to deal out or bestow in portions', from Latin distribuere.
items.cn: 最早记录为“分份给出或施予”，来自拉丁语 distribuere。

items.en: distribuere 'deal out, divide among' = dis- 'apart' + tribuere 'assign, allot, grant'.
items.cn: distribuere“分出、分给”= dis-“分开”+ tribuere“分配、授予、给予”。

items.en: tribuere comes from tribus 'a tribe, a division of the Roman people'. The origin of tribus itself is uncertain; one old suggestion connects it to tri- 'three', but this is not established.
items.cn: tribuere 来自 tribus“部落、罗马人民的区分单位”。tribus 本身的来源不确定；旧说之一把它联系到 tri-“三”，但未获证实。

items.en: The sense 'classify, arrange in order' appears, now obsolete.
items.cn: “分类、按序排列”的义项出现，现已废用。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across logistics, media, mathematics, and statistics, but the core act remains the same: one whole, many receivers.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词铺到物流、媒体、数学与统计上，但核心动作不变：一个整体，许多接收者。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stem tribuere or the spelling of distribute; the second is about verbs that also divide and give out.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词干 tribuere 或 distribute 的拼写，第二组看同样表示“分开并给出”的动词。

entries.definition: the act or pattern of spreading something out. It is distribute plus -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 分发；分布格局。它是 distribute 加 -ion。

entries.definition: a company or device that distributes. It is distribute plus -or.
entries.definitionCN: 分销商；分配器。它是 distribute 加 -or。

entries.definition: to give money or effort to a common fund. It uses the same tribuere with con- 'together'.
entries.definitionCN: 向共同基金给钱或出力。它用同一个 tribuere 加 con-“共同”。

entries.definition: to set resources aside for a purpose. It stresses the plan, not the handing out.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的划拨资源。它强调计划，而非逐份发出去。

entries.definition: to spread out and move apart. It fits the wind and seed sense but not the share sense.
entries.definitionCN: 散开并四散。它贴合风与种子义，不贴合“份额”义。

entries.definition: to divide something among people so each gets part. It is the everyday verb behind distribute.
entries.definitionCN: 在人与人之间分，使每人得到一部分。它是 distribute 背后的日常动词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin tribuere 'allot', the tribe as a unit of division, the distributive law, and the everyday pattern distribute something to someone.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 tribuere“分配”、作为分配单位的部落、分配律，以及 distribute something to someone 的日常搭配。

normal.en: Latin tribuere means 'to allot'. Distribute is to allot apart, giving each receiver a share.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 tribuere 意为“分配”。distribute 就是分开分配，给每个接收者一份。

normal.en: The word began with the tribe: the Roman people were divided into tribus, and to distribute was to divide among them.
normal.cn: 这个词始于部落：罗马人被分成 tribus，distribute 就是在他们之间分配。

normal.en: Place, not person, can be the receiver: wind distributes seeds, and a map shows where they landed.
normal.cn: 接收者可以是地点而非人：风把种子散布，地图显示它们落在哪里。

normal.en: In maths, distribute the 3 over (x + 2): the multiplier is handed to every term inside.
normal.cn: 数学里把 3 分配到 (x + 2)：乘数被发给括号内每一项。

normal.en: Supply chains use the same verb: a producer distributes goods to the points where they are sold.
normal.cn: 供应链用同一个动词：生产者把货物分发到销售点。

abstract.en: Distribution is a moral question disguised as logistics: who receives a share, and by what rule.
abstract.cn: 分配是伪装成物流的伦理问题：谁得到一份，按什么规则。

abstract.en: A whole becomes many without being destroyed: distribution multiplies presence while diminishing each portion.
abstract.cn: 整体变成许多而未被毁掉：分配扩大了在场，却缩小了每一份。

abstract.en: Every distribution implies a centre: something had to be gathered before it could be spread.
abstract.cn: 每一次分配都暗示一个中心：东西必须先被聚拢，才可能被撒开。

examples.en: Aid was distributed equally among the villages.
examples.cn: 援助在村庄之间平均分配。

examples.en: The species is widely distributed in tropical forests.
examples.cn: 该物种广泛分布于热带森林。

examples.en: Distribute the negative sign over both terms.
examples.cn: 把负号分配到两项上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地石吹牛特”——把地里的石头特意吹散给四邻 → distribute 分发、散布

root: 拉丁语 distribuere“分份给出”，由 dis-“分开”+ tribuere“分配”构成；tribuere 源于 tribus“部落”（来源存疑）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of distribute, all one operation seen at different scales: a whole is split so that many receivers, places, or terms each get a part.
sensesIntro.cn: distribute 的九个义项，是同一操作在不同尺度上的样子：一个整体被分开，让许多接收者、地点或词项各得一部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one whole dealt out into many portions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体被分成许多份发出去。

branches.en: DEAL OUT: each member, or each term in a bracket, receives its share.
branches.cn: 逐份给出：每个成员，或括号内每一项，都领到自己的份额。

branches.en: SPREAD: when the receivers are places, the shares become a pattern on a map or chart.
branches.cn: 铺开：当接收者是地点，份额就变成地图或图表上的格局。

branches.en: ALLOT: a rule divides the whole, whether by shares, classes, or categories.
branches.cn: 按规则分配：无论按份额、门类还是范畴，整体都被一条规则切开。

branches.en: REACH: goods and media travel from one source to many points of sale or viewers.
branches.cn: 抵达：货物与媒体从一个源头走到许多销售点或观众。

branches.en: LOGIC: a distributed term reaches every member of its class.
branches.cn: 逻辑：周延的词项抵达其类的每一个成员。

intro.en: Distribute is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -or, -ive, and the prefix re-, while the same tribuere builds tribute, contribute, and attribute.
intro.cn: distribute 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ive 与前缀 re-，同一个 tribuere 还构成 tribute、contribute、attribute。

latinIntro.en: Latin distribuere 'deal out' and tribuere 'allot' sit beside tribus 'tribe' and tributum 'tax, tribute'. The family is about dividing a whole among members.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 distribuere“分出”与 tribuere“分配”旁边是 tribus“部落”与 tributum“税、贡赋”。这个词族关乎把整体分给成员。

definition_zh: 多种多样的；形形色色的；不同的；多元的；各不相同的
definition_en: made up of many different kinds or types; not all the same
core_image: 一张桌上摆着来自许多国家的餐具，材质、形状、颜色全不相同
scene: 教室里坐满学生，肤色、母语和年龄都不一样。 One classroom held a diverse group of students — different skin colours, different first languages, different ages — all at the same table.
sceneCN: 这里 diverse 是「多元的、形形色色的」（第 4 个义项：由许多不同的人或物组成）；句意：一间教室里坐着多元的学生，肤色、母语、年龄各不相同，却都在同一张桌前。

pos.zh: 多种多样的；不同的；多元的

最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Of many different kinds
senses.definition: made up of things of many different kinds
senses.definitionCN: 由许多不同种类的东西组成
senses.example: The market sells diverse goods, from spices to radios.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场出售各种各样的商品，从香料到收音机。
senses.why: Latin diversus is the past participle of divertere, 'to turn in different directions'. Things that have turned apart are no longer alike, so the word names variety itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 diversus 是 divertere“转向不同方向”的过去分词。被转向不同方向的东西不再相似，所以这个词直接命名“多样”。

senses.title: Different from one another
senses.definition: not alike; each unlike the others
senses.definitionCN: 不相同；每一个都与其他不同
senses.example: Their backgrounds are diverse.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的背景各不相同。
senses.why: This sense looks at the members rather than the whole: a set is diverse when its items differ. The emphasis is on contrast within the group.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项看成员而非整体：一组东西的成员不同，这组就是 diverse。重点在组内的对比。

senses.title: Unlike something else (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, followed by from, meaning different from
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法，后接 from，表示“与……不同”
senses.example: Her manner was diverse from her sister's.
senses.exampleCN: 她的举止与她姐姐不同。
senses.why: The older construction diverse from treated the word as a plain synonym of different. Modern English has largely dropped it, keeping the plural, collective sense.
senses.whyCN: 较早的搭配 diverse from 把这个词当作 different 的普通同义词。现代英语基本弃用它，只保留复数、集合的含义。

senses.title: Heterogeneous in composition
senses.titleCN: 由不同成分组成的；多元的
senses.definition: containing people or elements of many different backgrounds or types
senses.definitionCN: 包含许多不同背景或类型的人或要素
senses.example: The city has a diverse population.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的人口构成多元。
senses.why: When the whole is made of unlike parts, the word describes composition rather than mere quantity. A diverse population is not just many people but many kinds of people.
senses.whyCN: 当整体由不同部分构成，这个词描述的是构成，而不只是数量。多元人口不只是人很多，而是人的种类很多。

senses.title: Including varied social identities
senses.definition: in modern usage, including people of different races, genders, abilities, and cultures
senses.definitionCN: 现代用法：包含不同种族、性别、能力与文化的人
senses.example: The company is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司致力于建设多元包容的职场。
senses.why: From the 1990s the word became a policy term. Diversity now names the presence of groups historically excluded, so the adjective carries a claim about fairness, not only variety.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪 90 年代起，这个词成为政策用语。diversity 现在指历史上被排斥的群体得以在场，因此这个形容词不只谈多样，也带着关于公平的主张。

senses.title: Rich in biological variety
senses.definition: of an ecosystem, containing many species or genetic types
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统中含有许多物种或遗传类型
senses.example: The coral reef is one of the most diverse habitats on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁是地球上最多样的栖息地之一。
senses.why: Ecology counts difference: species richness, genetic variation, habitat types. The word's core sense of many kinds becomes a measurable index of health.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把差异计数：物种丰富度、遗传变异、栖息地类型。这个词“多种类”的核心义变成可测量的健康指标。

senses.title: Differing in opinion or character
senses.definition: of views, temperaments, or approaches, not uniform
senses.definitionCN: 观点、性情或方法不一致
senses.example: The panel offered diverse opinions on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 专家小组对这项计划提出了各种不同意见。
senses.why: Disagreement is a diversity of minds. The same image of things turning apart applies to arguments, so a diverse panel is one whose members do not line up.
senses.whyCN: 分歧是心智的多样。事物转向不同方向的同一意象也适用于论点，所以多元的专家组，其成员不会排成一条线。

senses.title: A miscellaneous mixture
senses.definition: a collection of unrelated or miscellaneous items
senses.definitionCN: 互不相关或杂七杂八的一堆
senses.example: The drawer held a diverse collection of keys and buttons.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里放着杂七杂八的钥匙和纽扣。
senses.why: At its loosest, the word simply means 'assorted'. No principle is needed; the items merely differ. This is the everyday, non-technical use.
senses.whyCN: 最宽松的用法里，这个词只表示“杂七杂八”。不需要任何原则，东西只是不同而已。这是日常的非技术用法。

senses.title: Turned in different directions (obsolete)
senses.titleCN: 转向不同方向（已废的字面义）
senses.definition: the literal Latin sense, of things turned away from one another
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁语字面义：事物彼此转开
senses.example: In older texts, diverse paths might mean paths that branch apart.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本中，diverse paths 或指分岔的道路。
senses.why: This literal sense survives only in etymology. The physical turning apart is the ancestor of every modern meaning, from species to opinions.
senses.whyCN: 这个字面义只活在词源里。物理上的“转开”是全部现代义的祖先，从物种到意见。

intro.en: Diverse came from a Latin participle meaning 'turned apart'. Two spellings, divers and diverse, once competed; modern English split their jobs, leaving diverse for variety and divers for the old, plural sense.
intro.cn: diverse 来自一个意为“被转开”的拉丁分词。divers 与 diverse 两种拼写曾经竞争；现代英语把它们分工，diverse 管“多样”，divers 管古老的复数义。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'different, various', borrowed through Old French divers from Latin diversus.
items.cn: 最早以“不同的、各种各样的”义进入英语，经古法语 divers 借自拉丁语 diversus。

items.en: diversus is the past participle of divertere 'to turn away, turn in different directions' = dis- 'apart' + vertere 'to turn'.
items.cn: diversus 是 divertere“转开、转向不同方向”的过去分词 = dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”。

items.en: The spellings divers and diverse settle into different uses: divers survives as an archaic plural determiner, diverse takes the main adjectival work.
items.cn: 约 1700 年，divers 与 diverse 的拼写分化：divers 作为古旧的复数限定词残留，diverse 承担主要的形容词职能。

items.en: Diverse widens from 'unlike' to 'made of many kinds', and becomes common in biology and sociology.
items.cn: diverse 从“不相同”扩展到“由许多种类组成”，并在生物学与社会学中常见。

items.en: Diversity becomes a workplace and policy term for the inclusion of varied social groups.
items.cn: diversity 成为职场与政策用语，指不同社会群体的包容。

note.en: The first group shares the vertere root or the divers spelling; the second is about adjectives that also mean many kinds.
note.cn: 第一组共享 vertere 词根或 divers 拼写，第二组看同样表示“多种类”的形容词。

entries.definition: an older spelling and plural meaning 'several, various'. It is now archaic or literary.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的拼写，复数义为“好几个、各种”。现已古旧或仅用于文学。

entries.definition: the state of being diverse; variety. It is diverse plus -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 多样性；差异。它是 diverse 加 -ity。

entries.definition: to turn something aside. It comes from the same Latin divertere.
entries.definitionCN: 使转向一边。它来自同一个拉丁语 divertere。

entries.definition: of several different types. It stresses change and range, not social composition.
entries.definitionCN: 有几种不同类型的。它强调变化与幅度，不强调社会构成。

entries.definition: made of parts that are unlike. It is the formal, scientific word for diverse.
entries.definitionCN: 由不同部分构成的。它是 diverse 的正式、科学说法。

entries.definition: more than one. It counts items but says nothing about how different they are.
entries.definitionCN: 多于一个。它只计数，不说明差异程度。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin divertere 'turn apart', the divers/diverse spelling split, the modern policy sense, and the phrase a diverse range of.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 divertere“转开”、divers/diverse 的拼写分化、现代政策义，以及 a diverse range of 这一搭配。

normal.en: Latin vertere means 'to turn'. Diverse things have been turned away from each other, so they no longer match.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为“转”。diverse 的东西被彼此转开，于是不再相配。

normal.en: The older form divers is the same word: English once used both spellings, then gave them different jobs.
normal.cn: 较旧的 divers 是同一个词：英语曾并用两种拼写，后来让它们分工。

normal.en: A diverse population is not just many people but many kinds of people: composition, not quantity.
normal.cn: a diverse population 不只是人多，而是人的种类多：讲构成，不讲数量。

normal.en: Modern diversity is a policy word: it names the inclusion of groups once left out, not just variety.
normal.cn: 现代 diversity 是政策词：它指曾被排除的群体得以在场，不只是多样。

normal.en: In biology the word becomes countable: species richness is a measure of how diverse a habitat is.
normal.cn: 在生物学里这个词变得可数：物种丰富度衡量栖息地有多 diverse。

abstract.en: Difference is spatial before it is social: things must first move apart before they can be called unlike.
abstract.cn: 差异先是空间的，后是社会的：事物必须先分开移动，才谈得上不同。

abstract.en: Diversity is a relation, not a property: nothing is diverse alone, only in a set.
abstract.cn: 多样性是一种关系，不是属性：没有东西单独是多样的，只在集合中才是。

abstract.en: The same word describes a reef and a committee: variety needs no common measure, only unlike parts.
abstract.cn: 同一个词描述珊瑚礁与委员会：多样性不需要共同尺度，只需要不同的部分。

examples.en: The city is home to diverse communities.
examples.cn: 这座城市住着多元的社群。

examples.en: We need a diverse range of sources for the report.
examples.cn: 这份报告需要各种不同的资料来源。

examples.en: Tropical rainforests are biologically diverse.
examples.cn: 热带雨林生物多样性丰富。

dict_mnemonic.text: “带一份四”——带一份东西，分成四样，各不相同 → diverse 多种多样的

root: 拉丁语 divertere“转开、转向不同方向”的过去分词 diversus，由 dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”构成；同族有 divert、diversity、divorce。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of diverse, all resting on one Latin image: things turned apart. The turning can be physical, biological, social, or intellectual, but the result is always many kinds instead of one.
sensesIntro.cn: diverse 的九个义项都立足于一个拉丁意象：事物被转开。这个“转”可以是物理的、生物的、社会的或思想的，但结果总是许多种类而非一种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many things turned away from one another, so no two are alike.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多东西被彼此转开，没有两样相同。

branches.en: VARIETY: a set made of many kinds, from a market stall to a junk drawer.
branches.cn: 多样：由许多种类组成的集合，从市场摊位到杂物抽屉。

branches.en: CONTRAST: members differ from each other, from another thing, or in opinion.
branches.cn: 对比：成员彼此不同，或与另一物不同，或在意见上不同。

branches.en: COMPOSITION: a group contains people of many backgrounds, and policy names that inclusion.
branches.cn: 构成：一个群体包含许多背景的人，政策语言把这种包容命名。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: variety becomes countable as species richness and genetic difference.
branches.cn: 生物：多样性被计为物种丰富度与遗传差异。

branches.en: ETYMOLOGY: the obsolete literal sense of paths or lines turning apart is the ancestor of all the others.
branches.cn: 词源：道路或线条转开的已废字面义，是其余一切义项的祖先。

intro.en: Diverse is an adjective from a Latin participle. English adds -ly and -ity, and builds diversify and diversity from the same vertere family.
intro.cn: diverse 是来自拉丁分词的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ity，并从同一个 vertere 词族构成 diversify、diversity。

latinIntro.en: Latin divertere 'turn apart' produced diversus 'turned away' and diversitas 'variety'. The same vertere underlies divert, divorce, reverse, and convert.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 divertere“转开”生成 diversus“被转开”与 diversitas“多样”。同一个 vertere 还支撑 divert、divorce、reverse、convert。

items.meaning: the state of being diverse; variety
items.meaningCN: 多样性；差异（-ity 构成名词）

items.meaning: in various different ways
to make or become more varied
items.meaningCN: 使多样化（-ify 构成动词）

items.meaning: the process of becoming more varied
made up of varied parts
rich in living species
items.meaningCN: 生物多样的（bio- 表“生命”）

items.meaning: several, various (archaic)
items.meaningCN: 好几个的；各种的（古旧拼写）

items.meaning: to turn something aside
amusing or entertaining

latinEntries.meaning: to turn away, turn in different directions

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被转开的；不同的、各样的

definition_zh: 文件；公文；证件；文献；记录；（用文字或影像）记录；以证据支持
definition_en: a written or electronic record that carries information, or to record something in order to prove or preserve it
core_image: 一张盖章的纸被放进档案柜，纸上的字就是日后可以查证的凭据
scene: 律师把一叠纸页摊在档案袋旁，钢笔搁在签名处。 The lawyer spread a stack of documents on the table, each contract with a signature and a date, to prove the deal had taken place.
sceneCN: 这里 document 是「文件、凭据」（第 1 个义项：承载信息并可查证的书面记录）；句意：律师把一叠文件摊在桌上，每份合同都有签名与日期，用来证明那笔交易确实发生过。

senses.title: A written record of information
senses.definition: a piece of writing or print that carries information
senses.definitionCN: 承载信息的书面或印刷材料
senses.example: Please sign the document on the last page.
senses.exampleCN: 请在最后一页签署这份文件。
senses.why: Latin documentum first meant 'a lesson, a proof'. A document is a thing that teaches or shows: it carries knowledge that can be read later, which is why paper became its typical body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 documentum 最初意为“教训、证据”。document 是能教、能显示的东西：它携带日后可读的知识，因此纸成了它典型的载体。

senses.title: An official or legal instrument
senses.definition: a formal paper that records a legal act, identity, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 记录法律行为、身份或协议的正式文书
senses.example: The passport is the most important travel document.
senses.exampleCN: 护照是最重要的旅行证件。
senses.why: Law needs stable traces: a signature, a seal, a date. The document is the object that can be produced in court, so the word becomes a legal instrument.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要稳定的痕迹：签名、印章、日期。document 是能在法庭上出示的物件，因此这个词成了法律工具。

senses.title: A computer file
senses.definition: a file on a computer that holds text, data, or images
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中保存文本、数据或图像的文件
senses.example: Save the document before you close the program.
senses.exampleCN: 关闭程序前请保存文档。
senses.why: The digital age moved the word from paper to storage. A word-processor file is still a document because it still carries readable content and can be opened, edited, and sent.
senses.whyCN: 数字时代把这个词从纸搬到存储。文字处理文件仍是 document，因为它仍承载可读内容，可被打开、编辑与发送。

senses.title: A source or piece of evidence
senses.definition: a text or record used by historians or researchers as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 历史学家或研究者用作证据的文本或记录
senses.example: Historians compared letters and official documents.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家比对了信件与官方文献。
senses.why: Research treats texts as traces of the past. A document is not just information but proof that something happened, so the word shifts from 'paper' to 'evidence'.
senses.whyCN: 研究把文本当作过去的痕迹。document 不只是信息，而是某事发生过的证明，于是词义从“纸”转向“证据”。

senses.title: Record something in writing or media
senses.definition: to write down, film, or otherwise set down a record of something
senses.definitionCN: 写下、拍摄或以其他方式留下某事的记录
senses.example: The nurse documented the patient's symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了患者的症状。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: to make a document. It is used wherever a trace must be produced — medicine, science, law, journalism.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：制作一份 document。凡需留下痕迹之处都用它——医学、科学、法律、新闻。

senses.title: Support a claim with evidence
senses.definition: to prove or support a statement with records or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用记录或证据证明、支持一项陈述
senses.example: The report documents a sharp rise in costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告以证据说明成本急剧上升。
senses.why: Documentation is the backing of a claim. When a study documents a trend, it does not merely mention it but supplies the records that make it credible.
senses.whyCN: documentation 是对主张的支撑。一项研究 documents 一个趋势，不是仅仅提到它，而是提供使它可信的记录。

senses.title: Instruct or teach (archaic verb)
senses.definition: in 17c. usage, to teach or instruct someone
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪用法：教导或指导某人
senses.example: The old tutor documented his pupils in Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教师教学生拉丁语。
senses.why: The verb was first recorded in the 1640s with the sense 'to teach', directly from documentum 'lesson'. The modern 'record' sense came later, in 1711.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，义为“教导”，直接来自 documentum“教训”。现代“记录”义更晚，始于 1711 年。

senses.title: A lesson or warning (archaic noun)
senses.definition: in older usage, an example or warning that teaches
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：起教导作用的例证或警戒
senses.example: Let this be a document to you.
senses.exampleCN: 让这件事成为你的鉴戒。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: documentum in Latin is 'that which teaches'. English kept it briefly, then let the paper sense take over almost completely.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：拉丁语 documentum 是“教人之物”。英语短暂保留过它，随后几乎完全让位给“纸张”义。

senses.title: A film or photographic record
senses.definition: a film, photograph, or recording that preserves events as evidence
senses.definitionCN: 保存事件作为证据的影片、照片或录音
senses.example: The photographer spent a year documenting the village.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师花了一年记录这个村庄。
senses.why: Modern media extend the verb to images and sound: to document is to create a trustworthy trace, whatever the medium. A documentary is the noun for such a record.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒体把这个动词扩展到影像与声音：document 就是留下可信痕迹，无论媒介为何。documentary 就是这类记录的名词。

intro.en: Document began as a word about teaching, not paper. Latin documentum was 'a lesson, a proof', from docere 'to teach'. Only later did the written trace become the thing itself.
intro.cn: document 最初是关于“教”的词，而不是关于纸。拉丁语 documentum 是“教训、证据”，来自 docere“教”。后来书面痕迹本身才成了那个东西。

items.en: Borrowed as 'instruction, teaching' from Latin documentum; the sense 'written evidence' develops later.
items.cn: 作为“教导、教学”自拉丁语 documentum 借入；“书面证据”义后来才发展出来。

items.en: documentum 'lesson, example, proof' comes from docere 'to teach', related to doctus 'learned' and doctor 'teacher'.
items.cn: documentum“教训、例证、证据”来自 docere“教”，与 doctus“博学的”、doctor“教师”相关。

items.en: docere is traced to PIE *dek- 'to take, accept', also behind decent and decorate. The reconstruction is standard but remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: docere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *dek-“取、接受”，也见于 decent 与 decorate。这一重构是通行说法，但仍是重构。

items.en: The modern sense 'a written paper that furnishes evidence' becomes established.
items.cn: 现代义“提供证据的书面文件”确立。

items.en: The verb is recorded first as 'to teach, instruct', from the Latin noun.
items.cn: 动词最早记录为“教导、指导”，来自拉丁名词。

items.en: The verb's modern sense 'to support with documents, record as evidence' appears.
items.cn: 动词的现代义“以文件支持、作为证据记录”出现。

note.en: The first group is built from the same docere stem; the second is about words that also mean a record or a proof.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个 docere 词干构成，第二组看同样表示“记录”或“证据”的词。

entries.definition: a film record of real events, or relating to documents. It is document plus -ary.
entries.definitionCN: 记录真实事件的影片；文件的。它是 document 加 -ary。

entries.definition: the records that support something, or the act of recording.
entries.definitionCN: 支持某事的文件；记录行为。

entries.definition: a teacher or medical practitioner. It comes from Latin doctor 'teacher', from docere.
entries.definitionCN: 教师；医生。来自拉丁语 doctor“教师”，源出 docere。

entries.definition: a stored account of events. It is broader than document and need not be paper.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的存储记述。它比 document 更宽，不必是纸。

entries.definition: a sheet of material; informally, an official document. It names the body, not the proof.
entries.definitionCN: 一张材料；非正式指官方文件。它命名载体，而非证据。

entries.definition: a formal document that certifies a fact. It is a narrower, official kind of document.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某一事实的正式文件。它是更窄、更官方的一类 document。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin docere 'to teach', documentum 'lesson or proof', the paper and digital senses, and the verb document a process.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 docere“教”、documentum“教训或证据”、纸张与数字义，以及动词搭配 document a process。

normal.en: Latin docere means 'to teach'. A document is first of all something that teaches or shows.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 docere 意为“教”。document 首先是能教、能显示的东西。

normal.en: doctor and document share the same root: both come from the teacher's act.
normal.cn: doctor 与 document 共享词根：两者都出自“教”这个动作。

normal.en: Paper is only the usual body: a document is defined by carrying a record, not by being made of wood pulp.
normal.cn: 纸只是常见的载体：document 的定义在于承载记录，而不在于由木浆制成。

normal.en: The verb means make a record: nurses document symptoms, photographers document villages.
normal.cn: 动词意为“留下记录”：护士记录症状，摄影师记录村庄。

normal.en: Well documented means supported by traces: the claim is not just said, it is shown.
normal.cn: well documented 意为有痕迹支撑：主张不只是被说出，而是被展示出来。

abstract.en: A document is memory made portable: it lets a later stranger check what a past person did.
abstract.cn: 文件是可携带的记忆：它让后来的陌生人核查过去的人做过什么。

abstract.en: Teaching and proving converge: what instructs you also stands as evidence that the lesson existed.
abstract.cn: 教与证在此汇合：教导你的东西，同时也作为那堂课存在过的证据。

abstract.en: Every record is selective: a document preserves what someone chose to write down, and that choice is also evidence.
abstract.cn: 每一份记录都有选择：文件保存的是某人决定写下的内容，而这个选择本身也是证据。

examples.en: The treaty is a legally binding document.
examples.cn: 这份条约是具有法律约束力的文件。

examples.en: Researchers documented the decline in bird populations.
examples.cn: 研究人员记录了鸟类数量的下降。

examples.en: Keep all travel documents in one folder.
examples.cn: 把所有旅行证件放在一个文件夹里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “多客门特”——很多客人进门要出示的特件 → document 文件、证件

root: 拉丁语 documentum“教训、证据”，来自 docere“教”；同族有 doctor、doctrine、docile。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of document, moving from lesson to paper to evidence to record. The constant is a trace that can be read later: something that teaches, proves, or preserves.
sensesIntro.cn: document 的九个义项，从“教训”走到“纸张”，再到“证据”与“记录”。不变的是可被日后读取的痕迹：能教、能证、能保存的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trace that can be read later as proof or instruction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道日后可被读取为证据或教导的痕迹。

branches.en: TEACH: the oldest layer, where a documentum is a lesson or warning.
branches.cn: 教导：最古老的一层，documentum 是教训或鉴戒。

branches.en: PROVE: a paper with a seal or a text in an archive stands as evidence.
branches.cn: 证明：盖章的纸或档案里的文本作为证据成立。

branches.en: STORE: the digital file keeps the same function without paper.
branches.cn: 存储：数字文件不以纸为载体，却保持同一功能。

branches.en: RECORD: writing, filming, or photographing produces the trace that supports a claim.
branches.cn: 记录：书写、拍摄或摄影产出支撑主张的痕迹。

branches.en: INSTRUCT: the archaic verb returns to the root sense of teaching.
branches.cn: 指导：古义动词回到“教”的词根义。

intro.en: Document is both noun and verb. English adds -ary, -ation, -ed, and the negative un-, while the root docere also gives doctor, doctrine, and docile.
intro.cn: document 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ary、-ation、-ed 与否定 un-，词根 docere 还生成 doctor、doctrine、docile。

latinIntro.en: Latin documentum 'lesson, proof' and docere 'to teach' sit beside doctor 'teacher' and doctrina 'teaching'. The family is about instruction and the authority that comes with it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 documentum“教训、证据”与 docere“教”旁边是 doctor“教师”与 doctrina“教导”。这个词族关乎教导，以及教导带来的权威。
